research.dimension: SKL — official Anthropic guidance on authoring skills (SKILL.md), as of 2026-09-23 / Claude Code 2.1.280

claims.claim: Custom slash commands are merged into skills: a .claude/commands/x.md file and a skills/x/SKILL.md both create /x and behave the same. Skills add a supporting-files directory, invocation-control frontmatter and model auto-loading.
claims.quote: Custom commands have been merged into skills. A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy` and work the same way.
claims.implication_for_repo: A thin commands/<cmd>.md that only forwards to a skill duplicates it. The skill is already invocable as /plugin:skill and takes argument-hint and $ARGUMENTS, so fold the command into the skill.

claims.claim: In plugins, the commands/ directory is now described as 'skills as flat Markdown files', and new plugins should use skills/. Commands count toward the plugin's projected skill token cost.
claims.quote: Skills as flat Markdown files. Use `skills/` for new plugins
claims.implication_for_repo: The rewrite should retire plugins/*/commands/*.md (e.g. /new-plugin, /digest, /infographic) in favour of skills/ entries. Each extra command is another listing entry competing for the description budget.

claims.claim: In Claude Code every frontmatter field is optional and only description is recommended. Field names must match the documented table exactly, and an unrecognized field is silently ignored with no error.
claims.quote: All fields are optional. Only `description` is recommended so Claude knows when to use the skill. A field name must match the table exactly, hyphens included: Claude Code ignores a field it doesn't recognize without reporting an error.
claims.implication_for_repo: validate.py should whitelist field names (name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, background, hooks, paths, shell, metadata, license, compatibility), because a typo such as allowed_tools silently does nothing.

claims.claim: Outside Claude Code (claude.ai uploads, the Skills API, package_skill.py), only the six Agent Skills spec fields are allowed, and any other key is a hard error. Claude Code-only body features such as !`cmd` injection do not work there.
claims.quote: Unexpected key(s) in SKILL.md frontmatter: argument-hint. Allowed properties are: allowed-tools, compatibility, description, license, metadata, name
claims.implication_for_repo: If any repo skill will also be enabled on the claude.ai account (for Cowork, cloud sessions or routines), keep its frontmatter to the six spec fields. Otherwise, mark it as Claude Code-only in the plan.

claims.claim: The platform (API and claude.ai) docs treat name and description as REQUIRED. name: at most 64 chars, only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no XML tags, and must not contain the reserved words 'anthropic' or 'claude'. description: non-empty, at most 1,024 chars, no XML tags. This contradicts Claude Code's 'all fields optional' (SKL-03). The difference is by surface, not by date.
claims.quote: Cannot contain reserved words: "anthropic", "claude"
claims.implication_for_repo: Write both name and description on every skill, even though Claude Code tolerates omission, and have validate.py enforce the stricter platform limits so the skills stay portable.

claims.claim: The open Agent Skills spec requires name to be 1–64 chars of lowercase a-z, 0-9 and hyphens. It must not start or end with a hyphen, must not contain '--', and must equal the parent directory name.
claims.quote: Must match the parent directory name
claims.implication_for_repo: This matches the repo's existing rule (skill name == directory name). Add the no-leading/trailing-hyphen and no '--' checks to validate.py.

claims.claim: Claude Code appends when_to_use to description in the skill listing and truncates the combined text at 1,536 characters. The key use case therefore goes first. This per-skill cap is separate from the 1,024-char spec limit on description itself.
claims.quote: Put the key use case first: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage.
claims.implication_for_repo: Descriptions that pack trigger phrases and NOT-for boundaries into ~1,000 chars could move the trigger phrases into when_to_use (Claude Code-only), so the portable description stays short. Either way, lead with the core use case.

claims.claim: The skill listing (names plus descriptions) is capped at 1% of the model's context window by default (skillListingBudgetFraction 0.01; per-skill skillListingMaxDescChars defaults to 1536). On overflow, the descriptions of the least-invoked skills are dropped first, but their names stay. /doctor estimates the listing cost and /skill-doctor reports per-skill cost and usage.
claims.quote: The budget scales at 1% of the model's context window. When the listing overflows, Claude Code drops descriptions starting with the skills you invoke least
claims.implication_for_repo: Roughly 28 skills across the two repos, most with ~900–1,150-char descriptions, plus synced claude.ai skills, can overflow the budget. Rarely used skills would then lose their descriptions and stop auto-triggering. Measure with /doctor and /skill-doctor, and set shorter description targets in the plan.

claims.claim: Platform best practices say descriptions must be written in third person ('Processes Excel files…'), not first person ('I can help…') or second person ('You can use this…'), because the description is injected into the system prompt.
claims.quote: Always write in third person. The description is injected into the system prompt, and inconsistent point-of-view can cause discovery problems.
claims.implication_for_repo: Audit descriptions for 'you'/'I' phrasing. Most repo descriptions already use a third-person verb ('Interrogates…', 'Extracts…'), which should become the standard.

claims.claim: The agentskills.io guide (linked from the Claude Code skills page) instead recommends imperative phrasing addressed to the agent ('Use this skill when…'), a focus on user intent rather than implementation, and being 'pushy'. This is in tension with SKL-09's third-person rule. The two pages carry no dates, so which is newer is unknown. A compatible reading is: open with a third-person 'what' sentence, then add an imperative 'Use when…' clause.
claims.quote: Use imperative phrasing. Frame the description as an instruction to the agent: "Use this skill when..." rather than "This skill does..."
claims.implication_for_repo: Pick one house pattern and enforce it in the rubric: a third-person capability sentence, then a 'Use when …' trigger clause, then a short 'Not for …' boundary.

claims.claim: Anthropic's skill-creator (the source of the repo's evals.json format) says Claude tends to UNDER-trigger skills, so descriptions should be slightly 'pushy' and list the contexts in which to use the skill, even when the user does not name the domain.
claims.quote: currently Claude has a tendency to "undertrigger" skills -- to not use them when they'd be useful. To combat this, please make the skill descriptions a little bit "pushy".
claims.implication_for_repo: The existing trigger-phrase-heavy descriptions follow this advice. Keep that pushiness but control its length (SKL-07/08), and verify it with trigger evals rather than by adding phrases.

claims.claim: A description must state both what the skill does and when to use it, with specific key terms, because Claude picks from potentially 100+ skills using the description alone. Vague descriptions ('Helps with documents') are anti-patterns.
claims.quote: Include both what the Skill does and specific triggers/contexts for when to use it.
claims.implication_for_repo: Add a rubric item checking that each description has a what-clause and a when-clause containing concrete nouns the user would type (e.g. 'PubMed', '.epub', 'infographic').

claims.claim: The recommended description length is a few sentences to a short paragraph, which is enough to cover scope without bloating context across many skills. The spec's 1,024 chars is a hard ceiling, not a target, and descriptions tend to grow during optimization.
claims.quote: A few sentences to a short paragraph is usually right
claims.implication_for_repo: Repo descriptions cluster at 990–1,150 chars. Set a soft target (e.g. ≤600 chars) and a hard fail above 1,024 in validate.py. atomize-book (1,075) and ingest-slides (1,150) already exceed the spec limit.

claims.claim: Description triggering should be tested with about 20 realistic queries: 8–10 that should trigger and 8–10 that should not, the latter being near-miss negatives that share keywords. Run each query 3 times with a 0.5 trigger-rate threshold, split queries 60/40 into train and validation, iterate about 5 times, and choose the description by its validation score. Simple one-step queries may not trigger any skill, so they make poor test cases.
claims.quote: Aim for about 20 queries: 8-10 that should trigger and 8-10 that shouldn't.
claims.implication_for_repo: For sibling skills that overlap (intent-lock / decision-interview / plan-critique; concept-animation / ml-concept-lab; comprehensive-review / pubmed-research-note), write near-miss trigger evals that pit each against the others.

claims.claim: Keep the SKILL.md body under 500 lines and about 5,000 tokens: only the core instructions needed on every run. Metadata costs about 100 tokens per skill and is always loaded. Bundled files cost nothing until they are read.
claims.quote: recommends keeping `SKILL.md` under 500 lines and 5,000 tokens — just the core instructions the agent needs on every run
claims.implication_for_repo: atomize-book's SKILL.md is 1,274 lines and must be split into references/. Add a line check and a rough token check (e.g. chars/4 ≤ 5,000) to validate.py.

claims.claim: Reference files should sit one level deep from SKILL.md. When a file is only reachable through another referenced file, Claude may preview it partially (e.g. with head -100) and miss content.
claims.quote: Keep references one level deep from SKILL.md. All reference files should link directly from SKILL.md to ensure Claude reads complete files when needed.
claims.implication_for_repo: validate.py can parse markdown links in references/*.md and flag any reference file that links to another reference file SKILL.md does not link to directly.

claims.claim: Long reference files should open with a table of contents. The two Anthropic sources disagree on the threshold: platform best practices say over 100 lines, skill-creator says over 300 lines.
claims.quote: For reference files longer than 100 lines, include a table of contents at the top.
claims.implication_for_repo: Adopt the stricter 100-line threshold (skill-creator states '>300 lines') and have validate.py require a '## Contents' block near the top of any references/*.md longer than 100 lines.

claims.claim: Each pointer to a bundled file should say WHEN to load it (the trigger condition), not just that it exists.
claims.quote: "Read `references/api-errors.md` if the API returns a non-200 status code" is more useful than a generic "see references/ for details."
claims.implication_for_repo: Rewrite 'see references/…' lines as conditional loads, e.g. 'Before rendering, read references/design-system.md'.

claims.claim: Contexts that are mutually exclusive or rarely used together belong in separate files, so a task loads only the path it needs. Code can serve as both an executable tool and documentation, but the skill must make clear which role applies.
claims.quote: If certain contexts are mutually exclusive or rarely used together, keeping the paths separate will reduce the token usage.
claims.implication_for_repo: Split mode-specific branches (e.g. firecrawl paths A–F, vault-keeper's five jobs, atomize-book's EPUB/PDF paths) into per-mode reference files.

claims.claim: Conciseness is the default assumption: Claude is already very smart, so include only context it lacks. For each piece of content, cut it unless the agent would get the task wrong without it.
claims.quote: Only add context Claude doesn't already have.
claims.implication_for_repo: Rewrite passes should strip general explanation (what a PDF, PubMed or an RCT is) and keep project-specific conventions, gotchas and exact commands.

claims.claim: In Claude Code, a loaded skill stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost. The Claude Code docs say to state what to do rather than narrate how or why.
claims.quote: Once a skill loads, its content stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost. State what to do rather than narrating how or why
claims.implication_for_repo: Long rationale paragraphs in SKILL.md bodies (history of why a rule exists) should move to references/ or ADRs. The body keeps the rule itself.

claims.claim: Sources conflict on emphasis versus explanation. skill-creator and agentskills.io say reasoning-based instructions beat rigid ALWAYS/NEVER directives, and treat all-caps MUST as a yellow flag. Platform best practices, in contrast, show Claude A proposing 'stronger language such as "MUST filter"' when a rule is missed. The Claude Code docs (SKL-21) favour stating what to do over narrating why.
claims.quote: Reasoning-based instructions ("Do X because Y tends to cause Z") work better than rigid directives ("ALWAYS do X, NEVER do Y").
claims.implication_for_repo: House rule for the rewrite: give each rule a one-clause reason ('X, because Y'). Reserve MUST/NEVER for truly load-bearing constraints (never fabricate clinical facts, move→verify→delete order), since many emphasised lines dilute each other.

claims.claim: Match the degree of freedom to how fragile the task is. Use high freedom (text heuristics) when many approaches are valid, medium (pseudocode or templates) when a preferred pattern exists, and low (exact scripts, 'do not modify the command') for fragile, sequence-critical operations.
claims.quote: Match the level of specificity to the task's fragility and variability.
claims.implication_for_repo: Label sections by freedom level: sync, bump, delete and vault-drain steps are low-freedom exact commands, while report shaping and chapter structure are high freedom.

claims.claim: Avoid presenting several equal options. Give one default with a narrow escape hatch.
claims.quote: Don't present multiple approaches unless necessary
claims.implication_for_repo: Where a skill lists several engines or tools as peers (e.g. five search engines in pubmed-research-note), state the default engine and the specific condition for each alternative.

claims.claim: Do not put time-sensitive information in skills (e.g. 'before August 2025 use…'). Put the current method in the body and collapse deprecated approaches into an 'Old patterns' section.
claims.quote: Don't include information that will become outdated
claims.implication_for_repo: Dated incident notes ('found 2026-08-…', version-history asides) belong in CHANGELOG/MEMORY or an Old-patterns details block, not in the instructions Claude follows.

claims.claim: Use one term consistently throughout a skill, for example always 'field' and never a mix of field/box/element/control.
claims.quote: Choose one term and use it throughout the Skill
claims.implication_for_repo: Fix one glossary per repo (e.g. 'vault' vs 'hub', 'report' vs 'note' vs 'artifact', 'asset') and apply it across skills, since cross-plugin handoffs depend on shared terms.

claims.claim: Always use forward slashes in skill file paths. Claude Code also rejects plugin component paths that contain a backslash on macOS and Linux.
claims.quote: Always use forward slashes in file paths, even on Windows
claims.implication_for_repo: The owner works on Windows (e.g. ingest-article hardcodes C:\Users\User\Desktop\...). Move machine-specific paths out of descriptions and into config or env variables, and make validate.py flag backslash paths.

claims.claim: For complex multi-step tasks, give sequential steps plus a checklist that Claude copies into its response and ticks off, so it does not skip validation steps.
claims.quote: provide a checklist that Claude can copy into its response and check off as it progresses.
claims.implication_for_repo: Pipelines such as atomize-book, ingest-article, empty-vault and comprehensive-review should each open with a copyable progress checklist in place of prose step descriptions.

claims.claim: Build in feedback loops (run validator → fix → repeat, and proceed only after it passes). For batch, destructive or high-stakes operations, use plan-validate-execute: write a structured plan file, validate it with a script against the source of truth, then execute.
claims.quote: When to use: Batch operations, destructive changes, complex validation rules, high-stakes operations.
claims.implication_for_repo: Existing gates (validate.py, qc-gate.py, check-figures.py) fit this pattern. Make each skill say 'only proceed when X passes', and make vault-drain and sync operations write a plan file that is validated before execution.

claims.claim: A 'Gotchas' list is often the highest-value content in a skill: concrete, environment-specific corrections. It should live in SKILL.md, where the agent sees it before hitting the situation. Each correction the user has to make should be added to it.
claims.quote: Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md` where the agent reads them before encountering the situation.
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub's CLAUDE.md holds a very large gotchas corpus that loads every session. Move skill-specific gotchas (e.g. figure-extraction and sync traps) into the owning skill's SKILL.md, or into a clearly triggered reference file.

claims.claim: Scripts should solve errors themselves rather than defer them to Claude, and constants must be justified in comments (no 'voodoo constants'). The instructions must say whether Claude should EXECUTE a script (the common case, where only its output enters context) or READ it as reference.
claims.quote: When writing scripts for Skills, handle error conditions rather than deferring to Claude.
claims.implication_for_repo: Every scripts/ reference in a SKILL.md should read 'Run `…`' or 'See `…` for the algorithm'. Logic that agents currently re-derive in prose (e.g. manual char counts, YAML checks) belongs in a tested script.

claims.claim: Scripts built for agents must be non-interactive (no TTY prompts) and document themselves via --help. They should send structured data to stdout and diagnostics to stderr, return helpful errors and meaningful exit codes, be idempotent, offer --dry-run for destructive actions, and keep output size bounded.
claims.quote: Agents operate in non-interactive shells — they cannot respond to TTY prompts, password dialogs, or confirmation menus.
claims.implication_for_repo: Audit bump.py, route.py, validate.py and the learn-hub sync/purge scripts against this checklist. Most already dry-run by default, but add JSON output and --help where they are missing.

claims.claim: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is the skill's own directory, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} the plugin root, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} a persistent data directory, and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} the project root. They are substituted in the body and in Bash allowed-tools rules, so the same variable in both places lets a bundled script run without a permission prompt.
claims.quote: Using the same variable in both places lets a skill run a bundled script without a permission prompt.
claims.implication_for_repo: Replace relative or cwd-dependent script paths in plugin skills with ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/… or ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…, paired with a matching allowed-tools: Bash(${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/x.py *).

claims.claim: Argument placeholders are $ARGUMENTS, $ARGUMENTS[N] / $N (0-based, shell-quoted) and named $name from the `arguments` field. If no placeholder receives the arguments, Claude Code appends 'ARGUMENTS: <input>'. A literal $ before a digit or placeholder name must be escaped as \$.
claims.quote: To include a literal `$` before a digit, `ARGUMENTS`, or a declared argument name, such as `$1.00` in prose, escape it with a backslash: `\$1.00`.
claims.implication_for_repo: When folding commands into skills, use argument-hint plus $ARGUMENTS, and grep skill bodies for unescaped $<digit> in prose (dosing and price examples) that would otherwise be substituted.

claims.claim: !`cmd` (inline) and ```! (block) run shell commands before the skill is sent to Claude, and their output replaces the placeholder. Any non-zero exit aborts the WHOLE invocation (append `|| true` where non-zero is expected). Commands run in the session's cwd, are checked against permission rules (anything short of allow aborts outside auto mode), and never run for skills synced from claude.ai.
claims.quote: A failed command aborts the entire skill invocation, not just its own placeholder.
claims.implication_for_repo: Use injection for cheap live state (e.g. !`git status --short`, current version from plugin.json, the vault index), always with absolute ${CLAUDE_*} paths and `|| true`. Never use it for anything that should work when the skill is synced to claude.ai.

claims.claim: disable-model-invocation: true makes a skill user-only. Its description is removed from Claude's context, it cannot be preloaded into subagents or fired by scheduled tasks, and it is meant for side-effect workflows. user-invocable: false hides a skill from the / menu for background knowledge that Claude alone should apply.
claims.quote: Use this for workflows with side effects or that you want to control timing, like `/commit`, `/deploy`, or `/send-slack-message`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Candidates are empty-vault, release/bump flows and purge-style operations. Caveat: other plugins delegate to vault-keeper through the Skill tool, and disable-model-invocation blocks exactly that, so split destructive jobs into their own user-only skill.

claims.claim: allowed-tools only pre-approves the listed tools for the turn that invokes the skill; the grant clears on the next user message. It does NOT restrict which tools exist. disallowed-tools removes tools while the skill is active. Workspace trust does not gate allowed-tools.
claims.quote: It does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable
claims.implication_for_repo: Do not rely on allowed-tools as a safety fence. Use disallowed-tools (e.g. keep AskUserQuestion out of autonomous fallbacks, or Write out of read-only skills) or hooks, and keep grants narrow, since any repo checkout can self-grant them.

claims.claim: context: fork runs the skill as the prompt of a new subagent (agent: Explore, Plan, general-purpose or a custom type) that does NOT see the conversation history. It runs in the background by default (background: false waits for it) and only makes sense for skills that contain an explicit task.
claims.quote: `context: fork` only makes sense for skills with explicit instructions.
claims.implication_for_repo: Self-contained heavy pipelines (literature sweeps, coverage reports) are fork candidates. Interview or gate skills (intent-lock, decision-interview, plan-critique) must NOT fork, because they need the conversation and the user.

claims.claim: model and effort frontmatter override the session's model and effort level while the skill is active. The model override lasts for the current turn only and is not saved. With context: fork, model sets the subagent's model.
claims.quote: Model to use when this skill is active. The override applies for the rest of the current turn and isn't saved to settings.
claims.implication_for_repo: Consider effort: high on adjudication-heavy skills (comprehensive-review, pubmed-research-note) instead of prose pleas for thoroughness. Leave model unset unless measured, since values outside availableModels are ignored.

claims.claim: An invoked skill's rendered content enters the conversation once and is not re-read on later turns. After auto-compaction, only the first 5,000 tokens of each skill's latest invocation are re-attached, within a combined 25,000-token budget filled from the most recently invoked skill.
claims.quote: keeping the first 5,000 tokens of each. Re-attached skills share a combined budget of 25,000 tokens.
claims.implication_for_repo: Put standing rules (fidelity contracts, never-fabricate, handoff targets) in the first ~5k tokens of each SKILL.md and write them as rules that hold throughout the session. Anything past that point can disappear after compaction.

claims.claim: Skills can declare hooks in frontmatter using the settings hook format. A skill hook is registered when the skill is invoked and keeps running for the rest of the session, unless once: true removes it after its first successful run. The Claude Code docs recommend hooks for enforcing behavior deterministically.
claims.quote: Claude Code registers them when you or Claude invoke the skill and keeps running them for the rest of the session
claims.implication_for_repo: Rules that are currently only prose ('run validate.py before commit', 'never write vault files directly') could become skill-scoped PreToolUse or Stop hooks. Note that they persist beyond the skill's own turn.

claims.claim: The paths frontmatter field takes glob patterns. Claude then auto-loads the skill only when working with files that match them.
claims.quote: When set, Claude loads the skill automatically only when working with files matching the patterns.
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub project skills tied to file areas (e.g. sync-vault on vault/**, check-repetition on vault notes) could use paths to cut false triggers. Test first, because paths also narrows auto-loading for chat-only requests.

claims.claim: Evaluation-driven development: create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive docs. Find gaps by running Claude without the skill, build three scenarios, measure a no-skill baseline, write minimal instructions and iterate. The platform page adds that no built-in runner exists; that statement predates or ignores Claude Code's `claude plugin eval` (SKL-46).
claims.quote: Create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive documentation.
claims.implication_for_repo: Each rewritten skill should ship with at least 3 evals and a recorded with/without baseline before its body is expanded. A skill with no measurable delta over baseline is a cut candidate.

claims.claim: Claude Code's guidance measures triggering and output quality separately, running each realistic prompt in a FRESH session with and without the skill, because leftover authoring context masks gaps in the written instructions.
claims.quote: A fresh session matters because leftover context from authoring the skill will mask gaps in the written instructions.
claims.implication_for_repo: The rewrite plan must not accept 'it worked in the authoring session' as evidence. Verification runs happen in isolated subagents or new sessions.

claims.claim: Iterate with two Claude instances. Claude A (the expert) helps write and refine the skill; Claude B (fresh, skill loaded) uses it on real tasks. Observations from B go back to A. Also watch how Claude navigates the skill: unexpected read order, missed links, overused files, and bundled files it never opens.
claims.quote: Work with one instance of Claude ("Claude A") to create a Skill that is used by other instances ("Claude B").
claims.implication_for_repo: The rewrite workflow should read transcripts of skill runs. A references/ file that no transcript ever opens is either unneeded or poorly signposted (SKL-18).

claims.claim: Claude Code (v2.1.269+) has `claude plugin eval`. Cases live in <plugin>/evals/ as case.yaml or prompt.md plus graders/*.md. Each case runs 3 times, a no-plugin baseline is compared by default, and the run exits non-zero below a threshold, so it can gate CI. A `tool_used: Skill` grader measures triggering. Its format is explicitly separate from skill-creator's evals/evals.json.
claims.quote: Its case format is separate from the `evals/evals.json` file the skill-creator plugin uses.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's per-skill evals/evals.json (skill-creator format) cannot be run by `claude plugin eval`. The plan must either keep skill-creator for iteration and add plugin-level case dirs for CI, or convert. The two eval dirs would sit at different levels (plugin/evals/ vs skills/<s>/evals/).

claims.claim: The two published evals.json schemas disagree on the assertion field name. skill-creator's schema uses `expectations`; agentskills.io's 'Evaluating skill output quality' uses `assertions` for the same list of verifiable statements.
claims.quote: `evals[].expectations`: List of verifiable statements
claims.implication_for_repo: validate.py should pin one field name, `expectations` if skill-creator's scripts are the runner, and reject the other so evals do not silently go ungraded.

claims.claim: Write assertions after seeing the first outputs. Make them objectively checkable, not vague ('output is good') and not brittle exact-phrase matches. Require concrete evidence for each PASS, and remove assertions that pass both with and without the skill, since they show no skill value.
claims.quote: Remove or replace assertions that always pass in both configurations.
claims.implication_for_repo: Review existing evals.json expectations for ones the model satisfies without the skill (e.g. 'produces markdown'). Replace them with repo-specific checks such as a handoff to vault-keeper, a marked verdict line, or a safety banner being present.

claims.claim: `claude plugin validate <dir>` checks skills, agents and commands in a directory, including SKILL.md frontmatter that fails to parse. --strict treats warnings (unrecognized fields, missing metadata) as errors for CI. In this session, `claude plugin validate --strict` passed on the micky-psych-tools marketplace and on learn-hub/.claude/skills.
claims.quote: To find `SKILL.md` files whose frontmatter doesn't parse, run `claude plugin validate` on the skills directory
claims.implication_for_repo: Call `claude plugin validate --strict` from validate.py (or CI) in addition to the custom checks. Keep the custom checks for the rules the official validator does not cover: version parity, description length, line and token budgets, and the evals schema.

claims.claim: If SKILL.md frontmatter YAML is malformed, Claude Code still loads the body but with empty metadata, so /name works while Claude cannot match the description and auto-triggering silently breaks.
claims.quote: If the frontmatter YAML is malformed, Claude Code loads the skill body with empty metadata, so `/skill-name` still works but Claude can't match against your `description`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Frontmatter parse errors are a silent triggering failure. validate.py should parse YAML strictly and fail on errors rather than warn.

claims.claim: Local check: strict PyYAML (as used by skill-creator's quick_validate.py and package_skill.py) FAILS to parse the unquoted `description:` of several repo skills, because an inner ': ' sequence is read as a mapping. Affected: micky-psych-tools intent-lock, learn-hub ingest-article, concept-animation, ingest-infographic and ingest-animation. Claude Code's own loader and `claude plugin validate --strict` accepted them.
claims.source_url: local: python3 -c "yaml.safe_load(frontmatter)" over plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md and learn-hub/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md
claims.quote: YAML ERR mapping values are not allowed here
claims.implication_for_repo: Write every description as a quoted string or a folded block scalar (`description: >-`) so it parses under strict YAML (portability to claude.ai and the API). Add a yaml.safe_load check to validate.py.

claims.claim: Local measurement: learn-hub atomize-book SKILL.md is 1,274 lines with a 1,075-char description, and ingest-slides has a 1,150-char description. Both exceed the spec's 1,024-char description limit, and atomize-book is about 2.5× the 500-line body guidance. The next largest are firecrawl (384 lines) and ingest-article (378 lines).
claims.source_url: local: wc -l + yaml description length over /home/user/{micky-psych-tools/plugins/*/skills/*,learn-hub/.claude/skills/*}/SKILL.md
claims.quote: 1274 1075 name,description learn-hub/.claude/skills/atomize-book/SKILL.md
claims.implication_for_repo: Priority targets for the progressive-disclosure split and description trimming are atomize-book first, then ingest-slides, firecrawl and ingest-article.

claims.claim: Skills should refer to MCP tools by fully qualified name. In Claude Code, a tool from a plugin-bundled MCP server is named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>, and that full form is required in allowed-tools, permission rules and hook matchers. Bare-server patterns never match it.
claims.quote: Tools from a plugin-bundled MCP server include both the plugin name and the server key in their callable name.
claims.implication_for_repo: Skills that call PubMed, ClinicalTrials or Firecrawl should name the exact tools (e.g. mcp__PubMed__search_articles for a connector, mcp__plugin_firecrawl_<server>__… if bundled). The platform page's 'ServerName:tool_name' format is the API-side convention, not Claude Code's.

claims.claim: Skill names should follow a consistent pattern; gerund form (processing-pdfs) is suggested, noun phrases and action-oriented names are acceptable, and vague or generic names (helper, utils, data) should be avoided.
claims.quote: Consider using gerund form (verb + -ing) for Skill names
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's noun-phrase names are 'acceptable alternatives'. Keep them, since renaming changes /commands and routing, but require new skills to follow one pattern.

claims.claim: When names collide, a synced claude.ai skill loses the bare /name to any local, plugin or command entry and stays reachable only as /anthropic-skills:<name>. Both entries still appear in Claude's listing. Name comparison ignores case, spacing and dash variants.
claims.quote: When another command uses that short name, `/<name>` runs the other command, and the synced skill runs only as `/anthropic-skills:<name>`.
claims.implication_for_repo: This account syncs a claude.ai 'psych-paper-digest' skill (daily 8–12-paper digest) alongside the repo plugin of the same name (watchlist triage). Two descriptions for overlapping intents compete in the listing, so rename one or sharpen both 'Not for' boundaries.

claims.claim: Scope each skill as one coherent unit of work, like a well-designed function. Too-narrow skills force several to load and risk conflicting instructions; too-broad skills are hard to trigger precisely. Overly comprehensive skills can also hurt, because the agent follows instructions that don't apply.
claims.quote: Skills scoped too narrowly force multiple skills to load for a single task, risking overhead and conflicting instructions. Skills scoped too broadly become hard to activate precisely.
claims.implication_for_repo: Use this as the test for merge and split decisions, e.g. whether vault-keeper's five jobs form one unit, and whether intent-lock, decision-interview and plan-critique should stay three skills with sharply disjoint triggers.

claims.claim: Treat skills like installed software: audit every bundled file (SKILL.md, scripts, assets) for unexpected network calls, file access or tool use. Skills that fetch external URLs carry particular risk because fetched content can contain instructions.
claims.quote: Skills that fetch data from external URLs pose particular risk, as fetched content may contain malicious instructions.
claims.implication_for_repo: Skills that ingest web or PDF content (firecrawl, ingest-article, pubmed-research-note) should state explicitly that fetched text is data, never instructions, and keep allowed-tools narrow.

open_questions: Which description style is newer or authoritative: third person (platform best-practices, SKL-09) or imperative 'Use this skill when…' (agentskills.io, SKL-10)? Neither page carries a date, and GitHub history for agentskills/agentskills was not reachable from this session.
Is Claude Code's tolerance of unquoted ': ' inside description (SKL-51) a guaranteed behaviour or an incidental parser leniency? The docs only promise that malformed YAML loads with empty metadata.

The listing budget is '1% of the model's context window', but the override variable SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET is a character count. Is the default budget counted in tokens or characters? Run /doctor in a session that loads both repos to measure real overflow.

Do thin plugin commands/ entries and their target skills each take a separate listing slot (double-counting against the budget)? `claude plugin details` was not usable on an unloaded local plugin path, so this was not measured.

Is `claude plugin eval` generally available on this account? Its docs have troubleshooting entries for 'plugin eval is currently in early access' and 'currently unavailable'. Should CI adopt it alongside the skill-creator evals.json format?

How should destructive delegated skills (e.g. vault-keeper's empty job) be restricted? disable-model-invocation blocks Claude's Skill-tool delegation from other plugins, so a split into separate user-only skills may be needed.

Should repo skills that are also enabled on claude.ai (synced) restrict themselves to the six spec frontmatter fields, or be marked Claude Code-only? That depends on which surfaces the owner actually uses them from.

platform best-practices, verbatim: "Always write in third person. The description is injected into the system prompt, and inconsistent point-of-view can cause discovery problems." Good: "Processes Excel files and generates reports". Avoid: "I can help you..." and "You can use this...".

agentskills.io/skill-creation/optimizing-descriptions: "Use imperative phrasing. Frame the description as an instruction to the agent: \"Use this skill when...\" rather than \"This skill does...\"", plus "Focus on user intent, not implementation" and "Err on the side of being pushy". Nuance: the Claude Code skills page links agentskills.io (root and evaluating-skills), not this page specifically. The platform's own good examples ("Extract text and tables from PDF files... Use when working with PDF files") already have the 'what, then Use when...' shape, which supports the compatible reading.

anthropics/skills skill-creator SKILL.md, verbatim: "currently Claude has a tendency to \"undertrigger\" skills -- to not use them when they'd be useful. To combat this, please make the skill descriptions a little bit \"pushy\"." Its example ends: "...even if they don't explicitly ask for a 'dashboard.'"

platform best-practices: "Be specific and include key terms. Include both what the Skill does and specific triggers/contexts for when to use it." and "Claude uses it to choose the right Skill from potentially 100+ available Skills." It lists "description: Helps with documents" as a vague description to avoid.

optimizing-descriptions: "Keep it concise. A few sentences to a short paragraph is usually right... The specification enforces a hard limit of 1024 characters." and "Check that the description stays under the 1024-character limit — descriptions tend to grow during optimization."

The numbers are verbatim: "Aim for about 20 queries: 8-10 that should trigger and 8-10 that shouldn't", near-miss negatives, "3 is a reasonable starting point", "0.5 is a reasonable default", Train ~60% / Validation ~40%, "Five iterations is usually enough", "Select the best iteration by its validation pass rate". The last sentence overreaches. The page says a one-step request "may not trigger a PDF skill even if the description matches perfectly", but it also says to "Include single-step tasks alongside multi-step workflows". It does not call them poor test cases.
results.corrected_claim: Test triggering with about 20 realistic queries (8–10 should-trigger, 8–10 near-miss should-not-trigger). Run each 3 times with a 0.5 trigger-rate threshold, keep a fixed 60/40 train/validation split, iterate about 5 times, and pick the description with the best validation pass rate. Agents often skip skills for simple one-step tasks they can handle alone, so the most useful should-trigger queries need the skill but don't obviously name it. Still mix single-step and multi-step queries.

skills.md, verbatim: "Keep the body itself concise. Once a skill loads, its content stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost. State what to do rather than narrating how or why, and apply the same conciseness test you would for CLAUDE.md content."

agentskills evaluating-skills: "Reasoning-based instructions ... work better than rigid directives (\"ALWAYS do X, NEVER do Y\")" is verbatim. The 'yellow flag' wording is only in skill-creator: "If you find yourself writing ALWAYS or NEVER in all caps... that's a yellow flag", plus "in lieu of heavy-handed musty MUSTs". agentskills does not use that phrase. The platform page shows Claude A might suggest "stronger language such as \"MUST filter\"", but as a suggestion for the author to review (step 4 is literally "Review Claude A's suggestions"), not an endorsement. The sharper tension is with Claude Code's "State what to do rather than narrating how or why".
results.corrected_claim: skill-creator and agentskills.io prefer explaining the reason over rigid ALWAYS/NEVER directives. Only skill-creator calls all-caps ALWAYS/NEVER a 'yellow flag'. The platform page only mentions that a helper Claude might suggest stronger wording such as 'MUST filter' for the author to review, so it does not really endorse emphasis. The real tension is with the Claude Code docs, which say to state what to do rather than narrate how or why. A reconciliation: keep the why to one short clause.

skills.md confirms that injected commands run before the content is sent, that output replaces the placeholder, and that "A failed command aborts the entire skill invocation". It also confirms they run in the session shell's cwd, that anything short of allow aborts outside auto mode, and that they never run for claude.ai-synced skills on your machine (v2.1.228+). But 'any non-zero exit aborts' overstates it. The page says: "One carveout applies: Claude Code treats exit code 1 from search and comparison commands as a normal result and injects their output. Exit codes of 2 or higher fail even for those commands." The `|| true` advice is for "any other command you expect to exit non-zero". Also, synced skills keep local behavior in cloud sessions.
results.corrected_claim: !`cmd` (inline, only at line start or after whitespace) and ```! blocks run before the skill reaches Claude, and their output replaces the placeholder. A failed command aborts the whole invocation. With bash, any non-zero exit fails, except that exit code 1 from search/comparison commands (e.g. grep) counts as a normal result. Append `|| true` to other commands that may exit non-zero, such as check scripts. Commands run in the session's current cwd (use ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} in paths). They are checked against permission rules, and outside auto mode anything short of allow aborts. They are not run for claude.ai-synced skills in local (non-cloud) sessions.

The five steps are verbatim on the platform page: "Create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive documentation"; Identify gaps (run without a Skill), "Build three scenarios", Establish baseline, Write minimal instructions, Iterate. It also says "There is not currently a built-in way to run these evaluations." That note is about the API/platform surface. Calling it something that 'predates or ignores' claude plugin eval is the researcher's speculation: the page carries no date, and plugin eval is a Claude Code-only command (v2.1.269+). skill-creator's eval loop also exists.
results.corrected_claim: Evaluation-driven development: create evaluations before writing extensive docs. Run Claude without the skill to find gaps, build at least three scenarios, measure a no-skill baseline, write minimal instructions, and iterate. The platform page says there is no built-in runner for its JSON eval format. For Claude Code plugins, `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269+) and the skill-creator plugin now fill that gap. Their formats differ from the platform's example.

The quote is verbatim in skills.md (v2.1.233+), and --strict "Treat[s] warnings as errors and exit 1... such as unrecognized fields". But plugin-marketplaces says: "From a marketplace directory, Claude Code doesn't open the plugins' skill, agent, command, or hook files." So a marketplace-root pass says nothing about SKILL.md frontmatter. I re-ran it locally (claude 2.1.280): `claude plugin validate --strict .` in micky-psych-tools gives 'Validating marketplace manifest... Validation passed', only the manifest. I also ran it on each of the 14 plugins/*/ dirs, and every one passed. learn-hub/.claude/skills gives 'Validating components... Validation passed'. Caveat: a plugin-dir run does not check a plugin-root SKILL.md.
results.corrected_claim: `claude plugin validate <dir>` (v2.1.233+ for non-manifest runs) reports SKILL.md/agent/command frontmatter that fails to parse. --strict turns warnings such as unrecognized fields into exit 1 for CI. A run from the marketplace root checks only marketplace.json and never opens skill files, so CI must validate each plugins/<name>/ directory (and .claude/skills) separately. In this session, --strict passed on the marketplace manifest, on all 14 micky-psych-tools plugin directories, and on learn-hub/.claude/skills.

The audit advice is framed mainly for skills from untrusted sources.

missed_practices.claim: Use the platform's pre-share 'Checklist for effective Skills' as a ready-made rubric. It covers core quality, code/scripts and testing, including: at least three evaluations, tested with Haiku, Sonnet and Opus, and required packages listed and verified. It maps directly onto a per-plugin rewrite scorecard.
missed_practices.quote: Before sharing a Skill, verify: ... [ ] SKILL.md body is under 500 lines ... [ ] Required packages listed in instructions and verified as available ... [ ] At least three evaluations created [ ] Tested with Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus

missed_practices.claim: Test a skill against every model it will run on. Effectiveness depends on the model: Haiku may need more guidance, while Opus may be hurt by over-explanation.
missed_practices.quote: Skills act as additions to models, so effectiveness depends on the underlying model. Test your Skill with all the models you plan to use it with.

missed_practices.claim: Because the skill file is not re-read on later turns, write guidance that must hold for a whole task as standing instructions, not one-time steps. This matters for long multi-phase skills like atomize-book or comprehensive-review.
missed_practices.quote: Claude Code does not re-read the skill file on later turns, so write guidance that should apply throughout a task as standing instructions rather than one-time steps.

missed_practices.claim: In a plugin skill, the frontmatter `name` becomes the last segment of the command (/plugin:name). In a personal or project skill it is only a display label and the directory name sets the command. So a name/directory mismatch silently renames a plugin skill's command, and name == directory should be enforced for plugin skills.
missed_practices.quote: In a personal or project skill, `name` sets only the display label shown in skill listings, and the command still comes from the directory name. In a plugin skill, `name` sets the last segment of the command and the plugin prefix stays in place.

missed_practices.claim: `claude plugin validate` run at the marketplace root does not check any SKILL.md. CI must validate each plugin directory (and a `skills`-named dir for plugin-root SKILL.md files), or frontmatter parse errors go undetected.
missed_practices.quote: From a marketplace directory, Claude Code doesn't open the plugins' skill, agent, command, or hook files. To find errors in those files, see Validate a plugin or a directory without a manifest.

missed_practices.claim: When output format matters, give a concrete template or input/output examples rather than describing the format in prose. Keep short templates inline and move long or conditional ones to assets/.
missed_practices.quote: When you need the agent to produce output in a specific format, provide a template. This is more reliable than describing the format in prose, because agents pattern-match well against concrete structures.

missed_practices.claim: Ground a skill in real expertise and real traces: complete the task hands-on, capture the corrections you made, and read execution traces (not just outputs) to find vague instructions, instructions that don't apply, and menus without defaults. Don't generate skills from generic LLM knowledge.
missed_practices.quote: A common pitfall in skill creation is asking an LLM to generate a skill without providing domain-specific context — relying solely on the LLM's general training knowledge. The result is vague, generic procedures

missed_practices.claim: Procedures that have grown inside CLAUDE.md belong in a skill, because a skill's body loads only on use while CLAUDE.md is always in context. This is directly relevant to learn-hub's very large CLAUDE.md, whose many procedural gotchas are paid on every turn.
missed_practices.quote: Create a skill when you keep pasting the same instructions, checklist, or multi-step procedure into chat, or when a section of CLAUDE.md has grown into a procedure rather than a fact. Unlike CLAUDE.md content, a skill's body loads only when it's used, so long reference material costs almost nothing until you need it.

research.title: Official Claude Code plugin + marketplace structure

research.dimension: PLG — official guidance on Claude Code PLUGINS and MARKETPLACES (plugin.json, marketplace.json, layout, components, versioning, caching, validation, release tagging, team/project consumption)

claims.claim: plugin.json is optional; when present, `name` (kebab-case) is the only required field. Components are auto-discovered from default locations without a manifest.
claims.quote: If you include a manifest, `name` is the only required field.
claims.implication_for_repo: validate.py should not demand fields beyond name as errors; keep description/author/keywords as house-style warnings, not hard failures.

claims.claim: Unknown top-level plugin.json fields are ignored at runtime and reported by `claude plugin validate` only as warnings; wrong-typed known fields are load errors. `--strict` turns warnings into exit 1 and is the recommended CI mode.
claims.quote: Treat warnings as errors and exit 1 on them. Use in CI to catch issues the runtime tolerates
claims.implication_for_repo: Health check should run `claude plugin validate --strict` (per plugin and on the marketplace) before/alongside the custom validate.py, so typos in manifests fail CI.

claims.claim: Type errors on recognized fields break loading (e.g. keywords as a string), while `experimental` and `metadata` with non-object values are only warnings.
claims.quote: a `keywords` value that is a string instead of an array is a load error
claims.implication_for_repo: Any generator in plugin-creator that writes manifests must emit arrays for keywords/paths; schema-check with the official validator rather than re-implementing types in validate.py.

claims.claim: The full manifest schema includes displayName, version, description, author{name,email,url}, homepage, repository, license, keywords, metadata (free-form, unread), defaultEnabled, component path fields (skills, commands, agents, workflows, hooks, mcpServers, outputStyles, lspServers), experimental.{themes,monitors,evals}, userConfig, channels, dependencies, and `$schema` for editor validation (ignored at load).
claims.quote: JSON Schema URL for editor autocomplete and validation. Claude Code ignores this field at load time.
claims.implication_for_repo: Add `$schema` to every plugin.json/marketplace.json for editor checking; put house-only data (e.g. routing hints) under `metadata` rather than inventing top-level keys.

claims.claim: `claude plugin init` (CLI 2.1.280) scaffolds a skills-dir plugin with `$schema: https://anthropic.com/claude-code/plugin.schema.json`, version 0.1.0, a root SKILL.md with `"skills": ["./"]`, and optional skills/agents/hooks folders via --with; its skill template tells authors to put trigger phrases in the description.
claims.source_url: claude plugin init demo-plugin --with skills agents hooks (run with HOME=$(mktemp -d))
claims.quote: "$schema": "https://anthropic.com/claude-code/plugin.schema.json"
claims.implication_for_repo: plugin-creator templates can mirror the official scaffold ($schema line, skills/ layout) instead of a bespoke skeleton; use the CLI scaffold as the reference shape.

claims.claim: Version precedence: plugin.json `version` always wins over the marketplace entry `version`, silently. Official docs explicitly advise NOT setting version in both places.
claims.quote: Avoid setting `version` in both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry. Claude Code always uses the `plugin.json` value without warning, so a stale manifest version can mask a version you set in `marketplace.json`.
claims.implication_for_repo: The CLAUDE.md hard rule 'Version lives in two files' and bump.py's dual-write contradict current guidance; plan to keep version only in plugin.json (or omit both) and drop per-entry versions from marketplace.json.

claims.claim: Resolution order when version is unset: plugin.json → marketplace entry → git commit SHA (for github/url/git-subdir and relative-path sources in a git-hosted marketplace) → archive digest → 'unknown'.
claims.quote: The git commit SHA of the plugin's source, for `github`, `url`, `git-subdir`, and relative-path sources in a git-hosted marketplace
claims.implication_for_repo: For a single-owner, actively edited marketplace hosted on GitHub, omitting version entirely gives automatic commit-SHA updates with zero bump ceremony.

claims.claim: Explicit versions pin updates: commits without a bump are invisible to /plugin update. Commit-SHA versioning (omit version in both files) is the documented choice for internal plugins under active development.
claims.quote: Users get updates only when you bump this field. Pushing new commits without bumping it has no effect
claims.implication_for_repo: Decide per repo: explicit semver (keep bump.py, single-file) or SHA versioning (retire bump.py). Either way, never both files.

claims.claim: Plugins loaded in place from a marketplace added as a local directory ignore version pinning: edits apply at next session start or /reload-plugins with no bump.
claims.quote: For a plugin loaded in place from a local-directory marketplace, your edits to the source directory take effect at the next session start or `/reload-plugins`. You don't need a version bump.
claims.implication_for_repo: The owner's own dev loop (local-dir marketplace or --plugin-dir) never needs bumps; versions only matter for GitHub-sourced installs, which weakens the case for mandatory per-change bumping.

claims.claim: Validating a marketplace directory checks marketplace.json schema, duplicate names, path traversal, each local plugin's plugin.json, and warns on entry/plugin.json version mismatch — but it does NOT open skill, agent, command or hook files.
claims.quote: From a marketplace directory, Claude Code doesn't open the plugins' skill, agent, command, or hook files.
claims.implication_for_repo: CI must also run `claude plugin validate --strict plugins/<name>` for every plugin to catch broken SKILL.md/agent frontmatter; the marketplace-level run alone is insufficient.

claims.claim: A per-plugin validate run checks plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json, and frontmatter of skills/agents/commands; exit codes are 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 run error; --json emits a machine-readable report (v2.1.259+).
claims.quote: The command exits 0 when validation passes, 1 when it fails, and 2 when the validation run itself fails
claims.implication_for_repo: validate.py can shell out to `claude plugin validate --json --strict` and only add house rules (description length, routing, eval presence) on top, instead of duplicating schema logic.

claims.claim: All 14 micky-psych-tools plugins and all 8 learn-hub plugins currently pass `claude plugin validate --strict`; the learn-hub marketplace fails strict (exit 1) only because it lacks a top-level description.
claims.source_url: claude plugin validate --strict /home/user/learn-hub (and each plugins/* dir in both repos)
claims.quote: description: No marketplace description provided. Adding a description helps users understand what this marketplace offers
claims.implication_for_repo: Baseline is clean; add a description to learn-hub's marketplace.json and make strict validation a gate so the rewrite cannot regress it.

claims.claim: Only plugin.json belongs in .claude-plugin/; every component directory (skills/, commands/, agents/, hooks/, output-styles/, monitors/, bin/) and .mcp.json/.lsp.json/settings.json sit at the plugin root.
claims.quote: Only `plugin.json` goes inside `.claude-plugin/`. All other directories must be at the plugin root level.
claims.implication_for_repo: Current layout already complies; keep references/ and evals/ inside skill folders, not under .claude-plugin/.

claims.claim: A CLAUDE.md at a plugin root is not loaded into context, and a plugin validate run warns about it; instructions must ship as skills (or agents/hooks).
claims.quote: A `CLAUDE.md` file at the plugin root is not loaded as project context.
claims.implication_for_repo: Any per-plugin guidance that must reach the model belongs in SKILL.md/references; READMEs and CHANGELOGs are for humans only.

claims.claim: commands/ is the older flat-file format; docs say to use skills/ for new plugins, and custom commands have been merged into skills (both produce slash commands and behave the same).
claims.quote: Skills as flat Markdown files. Use `skills/` for new plugins
claims.implication_for_repo: Thin commands (/infographic, /animate, /digest, /route …) are candidates to fold into the owning skill's frontmatter (argument-hint, arguments) rather than being separate files.

claims.claim: Skills docs state commands were merged into skills; `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create /deploy, with skills adding supporting files and invocation control.
claims.quote: **Custom commands have been merged into skills.**
claims.implication_for_repo: A command that only says 'invoke skill X with $ARGUMENTS' duplicates what the skill's own /plugin:skill entry already provides.

claims.claim: Plugin skills are always namespaced /plugin-name:skill; frontmatter `name` sets the last segment, and the bare /name also works unless another command already uses it.
claims.quote: In a plugin skill, `name` sets the last segment of the command and the plugin prefix stays in place.
claims.implication_for_repo: Command names used in docs/ROUTING.md should be written in the namespaced form (/clinical-infographic:clinical-infographic or the chosen skill name) since bare names can be shadowed.

claims.claim: Invocation control for user-triggered workflows is done in skill frontmatter: disable-model-invocation (manual /name only), user-invocable:false (model-only), argument-hint, and named `arguments`.
claims.quote: Set to `true` to prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill. Use for workflows you want to trigger manually with `/name`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Replace thin commands with argument-hint/arguments on the skill; use disable-model-invocation for destructive flows like empty-vault if they should never auto-fire.

claims.claim: Claude Code truncates the combined skill `description` + `when_to_use` at 1,536 characters in the skill listing.
claims.quote: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's 1024-char description cap is a stricter house rule; if when_to_use is adopted, validate.py must cap the combined length, and key triggers must come first.

claims.claim: Path fields behave differently: `skills` adds to the default skills/ scan, while commands, agents, workflows, outputStyles, experimental.themes and experimental.monitors replace their default directory.
claims.quote: **Replaces the default**: `commands`, `agents`, `workflows`, `outputStyles`, `experimental.themes`, `experimental.monitors`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Rely on default directories and omit path fields; declaring `commands` would silently stop scanning commands/.

claims.claim: All component paths must be relative, start with ./ and use forward slashes; backslash paths are rejected on macOS/Linux.
claims.quote: All paths must be relative to the plugin root and start with `./`, except that the `skills` field also accepts `"."`
claims.implication_for_repo: Existing `"mcpServers": "./.mcp.json"` is correct; validate.py can reject any manifest path lacking ./ or containing backslashes.

claims.claim: Marketplace plugins are copied into ~/.claude/plugins/cache (unless loaded in place); components or scripts that reference files outside the plugin directory fail because those files are not copied.
claims.quote: Claude Code also doesn't copy files outside the plugin directory into the cache when it installs the plugin
claims.implication_for_repo: Skills that reach for the repo-root vault/ or sibling plugins via relative paths only work when loaded in place; the rewrite must make each plugin self-contained.

claims.claim: Symlinks inside a plugin that point elsewhere in the same marketplace are dereferenced (content copied into the cache); symlinks outside the marketplace are skipped. --plugin-dir/local-path installs keep only intra-plugin symlinks.
claims.quote: **Elsewhere within the same marketplace:** the symlink is dereferenced.
claims.implication_for_repo: Shared references (e.g. authoring rules, report templates) can live once and be symlinked into consuming plugins instead of copy-pasted, as long as they stay inside the marketplace repo.

claims.claim: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} changes on every update for copied plugins and must not hold state; ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (~/.claude/plugins/data/{id}/) persists across updates and is deleted on final uninstall.
claims.quote: For a copied plugin, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` changes when the plugin updates.
claims.implication_for_repo: Mutable state such as intent-lock's misreads ledger or psych-paper-digest's last_swept must move to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (or the project dir), not live under the plugin tree.

claims.claim: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/DATA are exported to hooks and MCP/LSP processes but NOT to the Bash tool; in skill and agent content the placeholders are substituted inline at load time.
claims.quote: They aren't present in the environment of commands Claude runs through the Bash tool, in the main session or in a subagent.
claims.implication_for_repo: SKILL.md bodies must write the literal ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} placeholder (substituted at load) rather than telling Claude to `echo $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in Bash.

claims.claim: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} resolves to the skill's own subdirectory inside the plugin (not the plugin root), for referencing bundled references/ and scripts/ regardless of cwd.
claims.quote: For plugin skills, this is the skill's subdirectory within the plugin, not the plugin root.
claims.implication_for_repo: Long SKILL.md files that point at references/*.md should use ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/references/... so progressive-disclosure reads work from any working directory.

claims.claim: A plugin-root settings.json supports only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys; unknown keys are silently ignored.
claims.quote: Currently, only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys are supported.
claims.implication_for_repo: Plugins cannot ship permissions/env defaults via settings.json; config like the firecrawl key must use userConfig or environment.

claims.claim: bin/ executables are put on the Bash tool PATH while the plugin is enabled, but claude.ai organization distribution rejects plugins with a top-level bin/.
claims.quote: Don't include a top-level `bin/` directory in any plugin you distribute through organization settings.
claims.implication_for_repo: If helper scripts are added, keep them in scripts/ referenced via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} to stay compatible with claude.ai sync (needed for cloud sessions).

claims.claim: Plugin agents honor name, description, model, effort, maxTurns, tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, omitClaudeMd, isolation (worktree only), color, experimental; hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode are ignored for security, and initialPrompt is unsupported.
claims.quote: **Not supported, for security reasons**: `hooks`, `mcpServers`, and `permissionMode`.
claims.implication_for_repo: If any plugin adds subagents (e.g. parallel study adjudicators), declare tools/skills in frontmatter and do not rely on per-agent MCP or hooks.

claims.claim: Plugin agents are scanned recursively and namespaced plugin:subfolder:name; agent `name` values cannot contain ':'.
claims.quote: `agents/review/security.md` in a plugin named `my-plugin` loads as `my-plugin:review:security`
claims.implication_for_repo: Refer to plugin agents by scoped name in skills and hook matchers (anchor as ^plugin:agent$).

claims.claim: Plugin hooks live in hooks/hooks.json (or inline in plugin.json), support command/http/mcp_tool/prompt/agent types, and should reference bundled scripts via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, preferably in exec form (`args`) to avoid quoting problems.
claims.quote: so each path is passed as one argument with no quoting
claims.implication_for_repo: If gates (e.g. intent-lock enforcement, pre-save checks) move into hooks, use exec-form commands and scripts under the plugin, never repo-relative paths.

claims.claim: Hooks that target a plugin's own bundled MCP server must use the scoped tool name; matchers on the bare server key never fire.
claims.quote: A matcher written against the bare server key never fires.
claims.implication_for_repo: Any hook or allowed-tools list referencing bundled PubMed/CT.gov tools must use mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__* names.

claims.claim: Plugin MCP servers (in .mcp.json at plugin root or inline) start automatically when enabled; their tools are named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>, and that full name is what permission rules, skill allowed-tools and agent tools must use.
claims.quote: The full form is `mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool-name>`
claims.implication_for_repo: Three plugins bundling the same pubmed/clinical-trials servers yield three differently named tool sets; consolidate the MCP declaration into one plugin (dependency) or reference tools generically in skill text.

claims.claim: pubmed-research-note, comprehensive-review and psych-paper-digest each declare identical HTTP MCP servers (pubmed, clinical-trials) in their own .mcp.json.
claims.quote: "url": "https://pubmed.mcp.claude.com/mcp"
claims.implication_for_repo: Candidate for a shared 'evidence-engines' dependency plugin (see PLG-37) or a single owner, avoiding duplicate servers and inconsistent tool names.

claims.claim: userConfig declares values prompted at enable time (string/number/boolean/directory/file; sensitive values go to secure storage); values substitute as ${user_config.KEY} in MCP/LSP configs and exec-form hooks and are exported to hooks as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>. Project-level pluginConfigs are ignored.
claims.quote: Use this instead of requiring users to hand-edit `settings.json`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Firecrawl's FIRECRAWL_API_KEY and vault paths could be declared as userConfig (sensitive for the key) instead of prose instructions about environment setup.

claims.claim: defaultEnabled:false ships a plugin installed-but-disabled, recommended for plugins that add cost or connect to external services; the marketplace entry's value overrides plugin.json.
claims.quote: Use this for plugins that add cost or scope a user should opt into, such as one that connects to an external service.
claims.implication_for_repo: Consider for firecrawl (paid external API) so installing the marketplace doesn't enable it silently.

claims.claim: plugin.json `dependencies` (bare names or {name, version semver range, marketplace}) are resolved and auto-installed; a manifest of only dependencies acts as a bundle.
claims.quote: When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically
claims.implication_for_repo: Encode the pipeline's prose couplings (pubmed-research-note/comprehensive-review → intent-lock, vault-keeper; empty-vault → learn-hub) as declared dependencies instead of 'run plugin X first' text.

claims.claim: Cross-marketplace dependencies are refused unless the root marketplace lists the target in allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn.
claims.quote: By default, Claude Code refuses to auto-install a dependency that lives in a different marketplace than the plugin declaring it.
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub-local plugins could depend on micky-psych-tools plugins (e.g. intent-lock) by adding `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn: ["micky-psych-tools"]` instead of vendoring copies.

claims.claim: Release tags use `{plugin-name}--v{version}` matching plugin.json; version-constrained dependencies resolve against these tags (for relative-path plugins, on the marketplace repo).
claims.quote: Tag each release as `{plugin-name}--v{version}`, where `{version}` matches the `version` field in that commit's `plugin.json`.
claims.implication_for_repo: If explicit versions are kept, add `claude plugin tag` to the release step so cross-repo consumers can pin ~x.y ranges.

claims.claim: `claude plugin tag` validates the plugin, checks plugin.json and any enclosing marketplace entry agree on version, requires a clean tree under the plugin dir, refuses existing tags, and supports --dry-run/--push.
claims.quote: Create a {name}--v{version} git tag for a plugin release, validating that
claims.implication_for_repo: bump.py can shrink to 'edit plugin.json version → claude plugin tag --dry-run'; the agreement check makes the dual-file rule unnecessary when the entry omits version.

claims.claim: marketplace.json requires name (kebab-case, not reserved), owner{name}, plugins[]; each entry needs name + source; optional top-level description, version, metadata.pluginRoot, allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn, renames. Missing description is a validator warning.
claims.quote: Each plugin entry needs at minimum a `name` and a `source`
claims.implication_for_repo: Entries can shrink to name/source/description/category/keywords; learn-hub needs a top-level description to pass --strict.

claims.claim: Entry display fields (description, keywords, author, etc.) override plugin.json values in listings; relative-path sources resolve from the marketplace root and must start with ./.
claims.quote: Paths resolve relative to the marketplace root, which is the directory containing `.claude-plugin/`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Description text duplicated in plugin.json and marketplace entry will drift (it already differs in both repos); pick one home, ideally the entry for listing copy and plugin.json minimal.

claims.claim: strict (default true) makes plugin.json the component authority with marketplace entries only supplementing; strict:false makes the entry the entire definition and conflicts with a plugin.json that declares components.
claims.quote: `plugin.json` is the authority. The marketplace entry can supplement it with additional components, and both sources are merged.
claims.implication_for_repo: Keep default strict mode; don't declare components in marketplace entries.

claims.claim: A plugin's name is its stable identifier; renames/removals should be recorded in an append-only top-level `renames` map so existing installs migrate (validate checks for cycles). displayName changes UI labels without breaking installs.
claims.quote: Treat `renames` as append-only history
claims.implication_for_repo: If the rewrite merges or renames plugins (e.g. folding decision-interview/plan-critique/intent-lock), add renames entries rather than just deleting catalog lines.

claims.claim: A project repo consumes another marketplace by committing extraKnownMarketplaces (and enabledPlugins keyed plugin@marketplace) in .claude/settings.json; applied only after folder trust; project enablement overrides user settings.
claims.quote: Register additional plugin marketplaces by name, so that people who open the repository, or everyone your managed settings reach, get the marketplace without adding it themselves.
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub can reference micky-psych-tools (github source) instead of keeping forked copies under learn-hub/plugins/.

claims.claim: Enabling an external-source plugin (GitHub/npm) in project settings does not install it for others; each user must run claude plugin install. Third-party marketplaces default to autoUpdate false.
claims.quote: Enabling a plugin from an external source such as a GitHub repository or npm package in a project's `.claude/settings.json` doesn't install it for other people.
claims.implication_for_repo: Consumption via settings needs a one-time install step documented, and autoUpdate:true on the extraKnownMarketplaces entry if learn-hub should track micky-psych-tools automatically.

claims.claim: Cloud sessions do not install plugins that a repo enables via enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces; plugins must be enabled on the claude.ai account (synced plugins). The repo's .claude/skills, agents, commands, hooks and .mcp.json do load because they are part of the clone.
claims.quote: A cloud session doesn't install the plugins a repository turns on under
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub runs heavily in cloud sessions: switching from vendored copies to marketplace consumption only works there if the plugins are synced via claude.ai (or kept as committed .claude/skills); the plan must pick per surface.

claims.claim: git-subdir plugin sources let one marketplace list a plugin living in a subdirectory of another repo (sparse clone), pinnable by ref/sha.
claims.quote: Use `git-subdir` to point to a plugin that lives inside a subdirectory of a git repository.
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub-local's marketplace could list intent-lock/pubmed-research-note/comprehensive-review via git-subdir pointing at micky-psych-tools/plugins/<name> instead of copying them.

claims.claim: `claude plugin marketplace add` accepts --scope user|project|local (where the declaration is written) and --sparse paths for monorepo checkouts.
claims.quote: Where to declare the marketplace: user (default),
claims.implication_for_repo: Use `claude plugin marketplace add safetymickky-ui/micky-psych-tools --scope project --sparse .claude-plugin plugins` from learn-hub to write the consumption config rather than hand-editing.

claims.claim: Folders under a skills directory with .claude-plugin/plugin.json load as <name>@skills-dir with no marketplace/install; project-scope ones need workspace trust, load only from the primary working directory, and background monitors don't load.
claims.quote: Any folder under a skills directory that contains a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest is loaded as a plugin named `<name>@skills-dir` on the next session, with no marketplace and no install step.
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub's project skills could be grouped into @skills-dir plugins under .claude/skills if namespacing/bundling is wanted, without a marketplace install step.

claims.claim: --plugin-dir loads a plugin (or folder of plugins, v2.1.265+) for a session; a --plugin-dir copy takes precedence over a same-named installed plugin; /reload-plugins picks up edits.
claims.quote: When a `--plugin-dir` plugin has the same name as an installed marketplace plugin, the local copy takes precedence for that session.
claims.implication_for_repo: Dev/test loop for the rewrite: `claude --plugin-dir ./plugins` from the repo root, no bumps or reinstalls.

claims.claim: `claude plugin details` reports always-on vs on-invoke token cost per component; for an uninstalled plugin it works via --plugin-dir. pubmed-research-note measures ~432 tokens always-on and ~6.4k on invoke, with 2 bundled MCP servers not counted.
claims.quote: Show a plugin's component inventory and projected token cost
claims.implication_for_repo: Add a token-budget report (plugin details per plugin) to the rewrite's acceptance checks so long SKILL.md bodies are measured, not guessed.

claims.claim: `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269+) runs cases from <plugin>/evals/<case>/prompt.md|case.yaml + graders/*.md with a no-plugin baseline; this format is distinct from skill-creator's evals/evals.json, and experimental.evals relocates the directory.
claims.quote: Its case format is separate from the `evals/evals.json` file
claims.implication_for_repo: Existing skill-level evals/evals.json (skill-creator format) do not run under claude plugin eval; the plan must choose to keep, convert, or add plugin-root evals/ cases (no path collision since current evals sit under skills/<skill>/).

claims.claim: The documented first diagnostic for a skill is a `tool_used: Skill` grader; Δ near zero with it failing means the description isn't triggering on natural phrasing.
claims.quote: The most common first finding is a `Δ` near zero with the case's `tool_used: Skill` grader failing, which means Claude isn't choosing your skill on natural phrasing.
claims.implication_for_repo: Description rewrites should be validated with a trigger eval per skill rather than by char-count heuristics alone.
