research.dimension: EVL — how to test and evaluate Claude Code skills and plugins (claude plugin eval, skill-creator evals.json loop, trigger/description evals, static validation), and how the repos' existing evals map onto them

claims.claim: Claude Code now has two separate, non-interchangeable eval systems: `claude plugin eval` (plugin-level, prompt.md/case.yaml + graders/*.md, CI-gateable) and skill-creator's per-skill `evals/evals.json` loop (in-conversation iteration). A suite written for one does not run under the other.
claims.quote: the skill-creator plugin below runs a similar loop with its own `evals/evals.json` format. The two formats aren't interchangeable.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's skills/<skill>/evals/evals.json files are skill-creator format only; a rewrite must pick a canonical system (or keep both deliberately) rather than assume one feeds the other.

claims.claim: `claude plugin eval` discovers cases as `<eval dir>/**/case.yaml` or `prompt.md` (+ `graders/*.md`), where the eval dir is `evals/` below the plugin root unless `--eval-dir` or the manifest's `experimental.evals` says otherwise. Installed CLI is 2.1.280; the feature needs >= 2.1.269.
claims.quote: Run eval cases (<eval dir>/**/case.yaml or prompt.md + graders/*.md; the eval dir is evals/ unless --eval-dir or the manifest says otherwise)
claims.implication_for_repo: Plugin-level suites belong at plugins/<name>/evals/<case>/prompt.md, not at plugins/<name>/skills/<skill>/evals/evals.json.

claims.claim: If no `<case>/prompt.md` or `<case>/case.yaml` exists under the eval dir in effect, the run reports 'No eval cases found' and exits 1. So running `claude plugin eval` against any plugin in this repo today finds zero cases: every existing eval lives in skills/<skill>/evals/evals.json, which is neither in the default evals/ dir nor a recognized case file.
claims.quote: No `<case>/prompt.md` or `<case>/case.yaml` exists beneath the eval directory in effect, or your `--case` and `--tag` filters matched no case.
claims.implication_for_repo: Adding `claude plugin eval` to CI before migrating cases would fail every plugin with exit 1 ('no cases were found' is an exit-1 condition).

claims.claim: KEY MAPPING (repo evals.json -> claude plugin eval): the repo's 15 evals.json files (11 in micky-psych-tools, 4 duplicated in learn-hub/plugins; 118 evals in total) all use the keys {id, name, prompt, expected_output, files, assertions}. The mapping is: `name` -> case directory `evals/<skill>/<name>/`; `prompt` -> prompt.md body; `expected_output` -> the human-only frontmatter field `expected_outcome` (note the different name) and/or the rubric body of `graders/criteria.md` (type: llm); each `assertions[]` string -> one `graders/<slug>.md` (regex / tool_used / tool_order / file_exists / llm); `files[]` -> fixtures inside the case dir exposed via case.yaml `context.add_dirs` (or a `scaffold_script`); `skill_name` -> the `input_match` of a `tool_used: Skill` grader; `id` -> no counterpart (drop). 'negative-*' cases -> `tool_used: Skill` with `min: 0`, `max: 0`, `arm: both`. A mechanical converter is feasible because every file has an identical key set.
claims.quote: "name": "negative-precise-one-line-request",
claims.implication_for_repo: Write a small scripts/evals_to_cases.py (or fold it into plugin-creator) that emits evals/<skill>/<name>/{prompt.md,graders/*.md}; keep evals.json only if the skill-creator loop is still wanted.

claims.claim: prompt.md frontmatter is strict: an unknown key is an error. The human-only 'what good looks like' field is `expected_outcome`, not skill-creator's `expected_output`, so copying evals.json keys into frontmatter verbatim breaks case loading.
claims.quote: `prompt.md` frontmatter accepts these fields. An unknown key is an error
claims.implication_for_repo: A converter must rename expected_output -> expected_outcome and must not emit id/files/assertions as frontmatter keys.

claims.claim: Cases can be grouped by nesting them under a directory that isn't itself a case, and filtered with `--case <glob>` and `--tag`. A non-default eval dir can be set in plugin.json as `experimental.evals` (a relative path of plain directory names; absolute paths and `..` are rejected).
claims.quote: To group cases, nest them under a directory that isn't itself a case
claims.implication_for_repo: For multi-skill plugins (intent-lock, vault-keeper, plugin-creator) use evals/<skill-name>/<case>/ plus `tags: [<skill-name>, trigger|negative|output]` rather than pointing experimental.evals into skills/*/evals.

claims.claim: `claude plugin eval init --bare <name>` writes a blank template without running anything: prompt.md with `max_turns: 10` and `allowed_tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]`, and graders/criteria.md with `type: llm`, `weight: 1`. Without `--bare`, init runs an interview that reads the plugin, proposes should/shouldn't-trigger prompts, designs graders, pilots them once, and writes one case dir per prompt (needs a terminal; CI must use --bare).
claims.source_url: claude plugin eval init --help (Claude Code 2.1.280); verified by running --bare in a scratch dummy plugin
claims.quote: Author an eval suite under the eval dir (evals/ unless --eval-dir or the manifest says otherwise) via an interview that sources inputs and designs graders. Use --bare <name> for a blank single-case template.
claims.implication_for_repo: plugin-creator's references/templates/evals.json should be replaced (or joined) by a prompt.md + graders/ template matching the --bare output, so /new-plugin scaffolds runnable cases.

claims.claim: There are exactly six grader types: regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists (free, computed from transcript/files), and llm, baseline (judge-model calls). There are no custom-code graders.
claims.quote: There are no custom-code graders.
claims.implication_for_repo: Python checks like validate.py cannot be graders; every deterministic assertion must be expressible as a regex over a file/last_message/trace, a tool-call count/order, or a created-file glob.

claims.claim: To check a build/test/script outcome inside a run, the documented pattern is to have the prompt ask Claude to run it and write the outcome to a file, grade that file, and assert the command ran with a `tool_used` grader whose `input_match` names the command.
claims.quote: have the prompt ask Claude to run it and write the outcome to a file, grade that file, and assert the command ran with a `tool_used` grader whose `input_match` names the command
claims.implication_for_repo: Skills whose correctness is enforced by a bundled checker (plugin-creator -> validate.py, atomize-book QC scripts) can be graded by having the case run the checker and regex its written result, with --allow-tools "Bash(python3 scripts/validate.py*)".

claims.claim: Recommended grader design is one grader on the result (final message or produced file) plus one on the process (tool_used or tool_order), so a case tells you both whether the answer was right and whether the plugin produced it.
claims.quote: Give each case one grader on the result, such as the final message or a produced file, and one on how Claude got there, such as `tool_used` or `tool_order`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Each converted case should get at least a skill-fired/tool-order grader plus an outcome grader; the current evals.json encode both in one prose expected_output that must be split.

claims.claim: LLM judges vary more on longer text, so long outputs such as generated files should be graded with regex over the file contents; keep llm graders for short outputs, with rubrics written as concrete PASS/FAIL conditions. An llm grader passes on at least two of three judge votes; the default judge is a small fast model (haiku), overridable with --judge-model.
claims.quote: Keep `llm` graders for short outputs, with rubrics written as concrete PASS and FAIL conditions.
claims.implication_for_repo: Long-report skills (pubmed-research-note, comprehensive-review, psych-paper-digest) should be graded by regex over the written .md for required markers (verdict block, per-study sections, citation/PMID patterns), not by a haiku rubric over the whole report.

claims.claim: Grader targets: `last_message` (default), `trace` (JSONL; regex sees every message, but an llm judge sees only the first 12 and last 12), `files` (list of created paths, not contents), `{source: file, path}` (contents of one file), and `mock_calls`. Regex over the trace must match JSON-escaped quotes (\").
claims.quote: A `regex` grader sees every message; an `llm` judge sees the first 12 and the last 12.
claims.implication_for_repo: Process assertions for multi-phase skills (intent-lock's silent Phase 0 then picker rounds, empty-vault's move -> verify -> delete) should be tool_order/regex-on-trace, never an llm judge over a long trace.

claims.claim: With `{source: file}`, PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP files are shown to an llm judge as images; other binaries (.pptx, PDF) are refused and must be rendered to an image or written out as text. `files` lists only created paths, and `file_exists` counts only files created during the run.
claims.quote: A PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP file is shown to an `llm` judge as an image. An `llm` judge refuses other binary files such as `.pptx` or PDF
claims.implication_for_repo: HTML-producing skills (clinical-infographic, concept-animation, code-explainer, ml-concept-lab) should be graded with file_exists on *.html plus regex over the HTML for contract markers (prefers-reduced-motion block, no external src/href, mandatory 'medications to avoid' banner), not a visual judge.

claims.claim: By default each case runs in two arms, with the plugin and with no plugin, and reports WITH, W/OUT and Δ. A case scoring 1.0 in both arms means the plugin isn't what made it pass. `--ablation none` runs one arm, roughly halving cost.
claims.quote: If a case scores 1.0 both with and without the plugin, the plugin isn't what made it pass.
claims.implication_for_repo: Use Δ as the release signal for encoded-workflow skills (intent-lock, plan-critique, decision-interview); a Δ≈0 case is either redundant or its graders don't discriminate.

claims.claim: In a two-arm run, every `tool_used` grader on `Skill`, and any grader marked `arm: with-only`, is excluded from the score in both arms and shown only as a with-arm 'plugin-fired indicator'. The exception is when every grader in a case is of that kind: they are then scored normally. `arm: both` forces scoring in both arms, which is the right setting for a must-not-invoke check (`min: 0`, `max: 0`).
claims.quote: Set `arm: both` on a grader to score it in both arms regardless, which is what you want for a "must not invoke the skill" check with `min: 0` and `max: 0`.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's ~17 'negative-*' evals become tool_used Skill min:0 max:0 arm:both; positive trigger cases need an outcome grader too, or their Δ comes only from the fallback rule and is inflated (the without-arm can never fire the skill).

claims.claim: The canonical trigger check is a `tool_used` grader on `Skill` whose `input_match` regex names the skill. It also matches the namespaced `plugin-name:skill-name` form.
claims.quote: This passes when Claude invoked that skill at least once during the run, including by its namespaced `plugin-name:skill-name` form.
claims.implication_for_repo: Use input_match '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?<skill>"' in every case; for plugins with two skills (intent-lock + misread-capture) this also asserts the right sibling fired.

claims.claim: The most common first finding is Δ near zero with the `tool_used: Skill` grader failing, which means the description doesn't trigger on natural phrasing. The fix is to edit the description and re-run. If the Skill grader passes but Δ is negative, suspect the judge (re-run with --judge-model sonnet and tighten the rubric) before the plugin.
claims.quote: A small judge model can mark a correct answer wrong because it's formatted differently from what the rubric describes.
claims.implication_for_repo: Description edits (the repo's 200-1024 char rule) should be justified by before/after trigger-grader results, not by char counts alone.

claims.claim: Each case runs 3 times per arm by default (runs: 1-50). A run's score is the (weighted) fraction of graders passed, and the case score is the mean over runs. The default --threshold is 1.0, so the command exits 1 if any case is below perfect.
claims.quote: The default `--threshold` is 1.0, so the command exits 1 when any case scores below perfect.
claims.implication_for_repo: A CI gate needs an explicit --threshold (for example 0.8) and grader `weight`s that make the safety-critical checks dominate (for example clinical-infographic's avoid-banner, empty-vault's no-delete-before-verify).

claims.claim: Runs are isolated: a throwaway home dir, working dir and config, with only the target plugin loaded. User settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, personal MCP servers, other installed plugins, memory and skills are all absent, and no project .claude/ or .mcp.json above the sandbox is read.
claims.quote: Nothing personal or project-level loads.
claims.implication_for_repo: micky-psych-tools' routing layer (CLAUDE.md 'route first' + ROUTING.md) and learn-hub's CLAUDE.md conventions are invisible during evals, so trigger results measure the SKILL.md description alone, and any convention a skill silently relies on from CLAUDE.md must move into the skill/references.

claims.claim: A case's `plugins` field lists the plugin directories under test, relative to the case directory, and defaults to the nearest enclosing plugin. The docs show only a single-path example (`plugins: ["../.."]`) for when auto-detection fails.
claims.quote: Plugin directories under test, relative to the case directory.
claims.implication_for_repo: Cross-plugin routing negatives (intent-lock eval 8 -> plugin-creator; pubmed-research-note -> vault-keeper/intent-lock delegation) either need sibling plugin dirs listed in `plugins:` (unverified that multiple load) or must be reduced to 'this skill must not fire' checks.

claims.claim: Run limits: max_turns defaults to 10 (up to 200) and timeout_seconds to 300 (up to 3600). Hitting the cap is recorded as a run error and usually lowers the score, so set it generously.
claims.quote: Turn cap, up to 200. Hitting it is recorded as a run error and usually lowers the score, so set it generously
claims.implication_for_repo: Multi-phase skills (comprehensive-review, pubmed-research-note, atomize-book) need raised limits or cases scoped to one phase (for example 'Step 0 gate fires', 'report skeleton written') instead of whole-pipeline runs.

claims.claim: Tool access in runs: only listed read-only tools (Read, Glob, Grep, NotebookRead, Skill, Agent, TodoWrite, Task*) are granted. Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch/WebSearch are removed unless granted with --allow-tools for the whole run. Granted Bash runs under the OS sandbox (home dir unreadable, network limited), and only allowlisted env vars and EVAL_* reach the child.
claims.quote: Built-in tools that need a grant you didn't give, such as `Bash`, `Write`, `Edit`, `WebFetch`, and `WebSearch`, are removed from the session, so Claude can't call them at all.
claims.implication_for_repo: File-writing skills need `--allow-tools Write` to be testable; learn-hub skills that need Supabase keys from .env.local or the network (sync-vault, ingest-*) cannot run end to end in an eval, so test their deterministic cores with unit tests (EVL-41) and eval only the agentic decision steps.

claims.claim: Each run starts in an empty workspace, and `@path` mentions in the prompt are not expanded. Fixtures come from case.yaml `context.add_dirs` (read-only dirs inside the case dir) or `context.scaffold_script` (bash that runs outside the sandbox and only with --scaffold). `context.history_file` resumes a saved .jsonl conversation.
claims.quote: Each run starts in an empty working directory, so put whatever the task needs in the prompt itself, or set up the workspace first.
claims.implication_for_repo: evals.json `files` (empty today in all 118 evals) map to evals/<skill>/<case>/resources/ + `context.add_dirs: [resources]`; misread-capture's post-delivery complaint cases need a `history_file` transcript to be realistic.

claims.claim: MCP servers declared by the plugin are never started by default. Mocks go in `evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md`, where <server> is the server name in the plugin's MCP config; tools without a mock file are unavailable. An `expect:` block validates the tool input and aborts the run with score 0 on violation. `type: agent` mocks answer via the judge model, and their recordings can be adopted into `mocks/.replay/` and committed for repeatable CI. `_tools.json` supplies the real tool schemas.
claims.quote: Tools with a mock file answer from it and are allowed without an `--allow-tools` grant, and a tool with no mock file isn't available to Claude.
claims.implication_for_repo: pubmed-research-note, comprehensive-review and psych-paper-digest each declare MCP servers `pubmed` and `clinical-trials` in .mcp.json, so their suites need evals/mocks/pubmed/search_articles.md etc. (fixed PMID fixtures). `expect:` can assert psych-paper-digest's windowed date filters; `mock_calls` graders can assert the right searches were made.

claims.claim: CI recipe: `claude plugin eval . --trust-plugin --json results.json --threshold 0.8 --model <pinned> --judge-model <pinned> --no-publish --max-cost-usd N`. Exit codes: 0 all pass; 1 below threshold, load error, no cases, or untrusted dir; 2 partial (cost ceiling or auth); 130/143 interrupted/terminated. Pin both models so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression.
claims.quote: Pin it in CI so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression
claims.implication_for_repo: Add an opt-in `scripts/eval.sh <plugin>` wrapper with pinned models and a cost ceiling next to validate.py; keep it out of the every-commit health check because it spends model usage.

claims.claim: Each run writes `<eval dir>/results/<timestamp>/{aggregate-result.json, report.html}`, and results/ should be gitignored. aggregate-result.json is `schemaVersion: 1` with camelCase fields (aggregates.overallScore, casesPassed, meanDelta, cases[].aggregates.delta, partial). On a claude.ai subscription the HTML report is published as a private artifact by default unless --no-publish is passed. The Artifact tool is off inside runs.
claims.quote: results/               # written by each run; add to .gitignore
claims.implication_for_repo: micky-psych-tools/.gitignore currently holds only __pycache__/, *.pyc, .DS_Store, so add `plugins/*/evals/results/`. Skills that end by publishing an artifact can only be graded on what they write before that step.

claims.claim: Evals cost real model usage: about cases × runs agent runs per arm, doubled for the baseline, plus three judge calls per llm/baseline grader per run. For cheap iteration, run one case, one run, one arm; for every-change CI suites, use only free graders and `--ablation none` where Δ isn't needed.
claims.quote: To keep costs predictable, give quick every-change suites only graders that don't call a judge, use `--ablation none` where you don't need `Δ`
claims.implication_for_repo: Converting all 118 existing evals at the defaults (3 runs × 2 arms) means ~700 agent runs per full pass, so tag a small `smoke` subset per plugin (regex/tool_used only) and reserve full two-arm runs for releases/bumps.

claims.claim: skill-creator's evals.json schema: {skill_name, evals: [{id, prompt, expected_output, files, expectations|assertions}]}. The field name for checks is inconsistent across Anthropic sources: skill-creator's references/schemas.md and its aggregate_benchmark.py (which reads grading.json) use `expectations`, while skill-creator SKILL.md and agentskills.io use `assertions` (agentskills' grading.json uses `assertion_results`).
claims.quote: - `evals[].expectations`: List of verifiable statements
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo uses `assertions` (the agentskills/SKILL.md spelling). If the skill-creator scripts are used, the grading.json the grader writes must still use `expectations` with text/passed/evidence, or the viewer shows empty values.

claims.claim: In the skill-creator loop, prompts are written first and assertions are drafted while the first runs execute, after seeing real outputs. In the repo, all 118 evals across 15 evals.json files have `"assertions": []` and `"files": []`, and validate.py only checks that evals.json parses as JSON. So no eval in either repo has ever been graded or run through the loop.
claims.quote: Save test cases to `evals/evals.json`. Don't write assertions yet — just the prompts.
claims.implication_for_repo: The existing evals are prompt inventories, not tests. The rewrite plan should budget one real run per skill to produce assertions/graders before claiming eval coverage, and validate.py should fail an evals.json whose assertions are all empty (or cases with no graders).

claims.claim: skill-creator run protocol: for each test case, spawn the with-skill and baseline subagents in the same turn. For a new skill the baseline is no skill; when improving an existing skill, snapshot the old version first and use it as the baseline (old_skill/). Results go in <skill>-workspace/iteration-N/eval-<name>/.
claims.quote: Before editing, snapshot the skill (`cp -r <skill-path> <workspace>/skill-snapshot/`), then point the baseline subagent at the snapshot.
claims.implication_for_repo: For the rewrite itself, the right baseline is the CURRENT SKILL.md (old-version snapshot), not no-skill, so a rewrite can be shown not to regress before it replaces the long existing skills.

claims.claim: skill-creator benchmark: aggregate_benchmark.py produces benchmark.json/.md with pass_rate, time_seconds and tokens per configuration (mean ± stddev) plus the delta. Token and duration data must be captured from each subagent's completion notification immediately, because it isn't persisted anywhere else.
claims.quote: This produces `benchmark.json` and `benchmark.md` with pass_rate, time, and tokens for each configuration, with mean ± stddev and the delta.
claims.implication_for_repo: Long skills should be judged on the pass-rate delta against the token/time overhead they add; a skill that doubles tokens for a small pass-rate gain is a candidate for trimming.

claims.claim: Analyze results beyond the aggregates: remove or replace assertions that always pass in both configurations (non-discriminating); investigate ones that always fail in both; treat high stddev as either flaky evals or ambiguous instructions; read transcripts for time/token outliers.
claims.quote: Remove or replace assertions that always pass in both configurations.
claims.implication_for_repo: When converting expected_output prose into graders, drop checks the base model already satisfies (for example 'responds in Thai'), which would inflate WITH scores without showing the skill's value.

claims.claim: Assertion quality: good assertions are programmatically verifiable, specific and observable, or countable. Weak ones are vague ('output is good') or brittle exact-phrase checks. Graders must require concrete evidence for a PASS, and should also critique the evals, since a passing grade on a weak assertion creates false confidence.
claims.quote: A passing grade on a weak assertion is worse than useless — it creates false confidence.
claims.implication_for_repo: Regex graders should target structural markers the skill contract defines (headings, marker blocks, file names), not exact prose; the repo's expected_output strings mix several checks and need splitting into one discriminating grader each.

claims.claim: Subjective qualities (style, visual design) are better caught by human review than forced into pass/fail assertions. skill-creator's eval viewer (eval-viewer/generate_review.py) shows the outputs and benchmark and collects per-case feedback into feedback.json; `--static <path>` writes a standalone HTML for headless/remote environments.
claims.quote: use `--static <output_path>` to write a standalone HTML file instead of starting a server.
claims.implication_for_repo: Visual skills (clinical-infographic, concept-animation, ml-concept-lab, code-explainer) should combine regex contract graders with a human-review pass, since no plugin-eval grader can judge an HTML page's rendered design.

claims.claim: For 'is the new version better?', skill-creator offers a blind A/B: a comparator agent judges two outputs without knowing which version produced which, and an analyzer explains why the winner won.
claims.quote: runs a blind A/B between two versions of the skill so you can confirm an edit is an improvement before committing it
claims.implication_for_repo: Use blind A/B (old SKILL.md vs rewritten SKILL.md) as the acceptance gate for each rewritten skill whose value is holistic (report quality) rather than assertion-shaped.

claims.claim: Trigger/description evals: about 20 realistic queries (8-10 should-trigger, 8-10 should-not). The most valuable negatives are near misses that share keywords but need something else, not obviously irrelevant prompts. Queries should carry concrete detail (paths, context, casual phrasing).
claims.quote: the most valuable ones are the near-misses — queries that share keywords or concepts with the skill but actually need something different.
claims.implication_for_repo: This repo's plugins overlap heavily (intent-lock / decision-interview / plan-critique; pubmed-research-note / comprehensive-review / psych-paper-digest; concept-animation / ml-concept-lab). Each needs near-miss negatives drawn from its siblings' territory, which the current evals only partly have (0 negatives in 4 of 11 files).

claims.claim: Claude consults a skill only for tasks it can't easily handle on its own. Simple one-step queries may not trigger a well-matching skill, so trigger-eval queries must be substantive, multi-step or specialized.
claims.quote: Claude only consults skills for tasks it can't easily handle on its own — simple, one-step queries like "read this PDF" may not trigger a skill even if the description matches perfectly
claims.implication_for_repo: Positive trigger cases for gate skills (intent-lock, decision-interview) must present genuinely ambiguous, costly builds; trivial negatives like 'rename usrId to userId' pass for free and discriminate little.

claims.claim: The description-optimization loop (skill-creator scripts/run_loop.py) splits the query set 60% train / 40% held-out, runs each query 3 times with a 0.5 trigger-rate threshold, proposes description edits from train failures only (up to 5 iterations), and selects `best_description` by held-out score to avoid overfitting.
claims.quote: returns JSON with `best_description` — selected by test score rather than train score to avoid overfitting.
claims.implication_for_repo: Description rewrites should be run through this loop (or an equivalent held-out check), not tuned by adding the exact keywords of failed prompts, which agentskills.io calls overfitting.

claims.claim: skill-creator's trigger runner doesn't install the plugin. It writes a temporary command file into the project's .claude/commands/ so the description shows up in the skill listing, then runs `claude -p` with the raw query. It therefore tests the description in the user's live environment, alongside their other skills, whereas plugin eval tests it in isolation.
claims.quote:
Creates a command file in .claude/commands/ so it appears in Claude's
    available_skills list, then runs `claude -p` with the raw query.
claims.implication_for_repo: The two tools answer different trigger questions: plugin eval shows whether the description alone can win, and the skill-creator loop shows whether it wins against the owner's real installed marketplace of ~13 sibling plugins. The latter is the realistic routing test for this repo.

claims.claim: The skill listing is budgeted at 1% of the context window, and each entry's description + when_to_use is capped at 1,536 chars. When the listing overflows, descriptions of the least-invoked skills are shortened first. /doctor estimates the listing's cost, and /skill-doctor (>= 2.1.252) reports each skill's context cost and usage and flags skills that have never been invoked.
claims.quote: It flags skills in the listing that have never been invoked and says where to turn them off.
claims.implication_for_repo: Isolated plugin evals can't reproduce listing-budget truncation, so use /skill-doctor on the owner's real setup as production telemetry (which of the ~20 skills are never invoked) to prioritise the rewrite. /skill-doctor is not available over Remote Control.

claims.claim: Deterministic logic bundled with a skill should be verified by scripts or unit tests rather than LLM judgment. skill-creator says to write and run a script for programmatically checkable assertions. learn-hub already unit-tests atomize-book's Python helpers with stdlib unittest, outside `npm test`.
claims.quote: The `atomize-book` skill's Python helpers are tested too, and `npm test` does NOT run
claims.implication_for_repo: Keep a three-layer test stack: (1) static validation, (2) unit tests for scripts/ inside skills, (3) behavioural evals. Wire layer 2 into the health check explicitly, since npm test and validate.py don't run it.

claims.claim: `claude plugin validate <path>` statically checks plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json and the frontmatter of skills/agents/commands in default dirs. `--strict` turns warnings into errors (for CI) and `--json` emits a machine-readable report. Run on a marketplace dir, it also validates each local plugin's plugin.json and warns when the marketplace entry's version doesn't match plugin.json. The docs present this as the syntax/schema check, as opposed to behaviour evals.
claims.quote: it also validates that plugin's own `plugin.json` and warns when the entry's `version` doesn't match the one in `plugin.json`.
claims.implication_for_repo: scripts/validate.py duplicates part of this (manifest/catalog version equality, frontmatter). Run `claude plugin validate . --strict` plus a per-plugin run in the health check, and keep validate.py only for repo-specific rules (200-1024 char descriptions, name==dir, ROUTING.md freshness, evals coverage).

claims.claim: Official measurement advice is to check triggering and output quality separately, in fresh sessions, against a baseline with the skill disabled. Leftover authoring context masks gaps in the written instructions.
claims.quote: A fresh session matters because leftover context from authoring the skill will mask gaps in the written instructions.
claims.implication_for_repo: Rewrite verification must not be done in the same session that rewrote the skill; use plugin eval or skill-creator subagents (fresh context) for every rewritten skill.

claims.claim: Evaluation-driven development: run Claude without the skill on representative tasks, write about three evaluations targeting the observed gaps, measure the baseline, then write only the minimal instructions needed. The checklist also asks for testing with Haiku, Sonnet and Opus.
claims.quote: Create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive documentation.
claims.implication_for_repo: For each long SKILL.md, the rewrite should start from a without-skill baseline run and cut sections that close no observed gap. Use `--model` to run the smoke suite on at least two model tiers.

claims.claim: Doc conflict: the platform best-practices page (undated) says there is no built-in way to run skill evaluations, while the newer Claude Code docs ship `claude plugin eval` (released v2.1.269, week of Sept 7-11 2026) and skill-creator's eval/benchmark modes (announced March 3, 2026). The newer Claude Code docs supersede the older statement for plugin-packaged skills.
claims.quote: There is not currently a built-in way to run these evaluations. Users can create their own evaluation system.
claims.implication_for_repo: Prefer the built-in `claude plugin eval` for plugins over growing a custom eval harness; the best-practices JSON shape (skills/query/files/expected_behavior) is illustrative only.

claims.claim: `claude plugin eval` requires a plugin manifest (plugin.json) or a skills-directory plugin (a folder under a skills dir containing .claude-plugin/plugin.json, loaded as <name>@skills-dir). Plain project skills in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md without a manifest are not a valid target. The docs' alternative for them is the skill-creator loop or fresh-session with/without comparisons.
claims.quote: A plugin directory with a `plugin.json` or `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, or a
claims.implication_for_repo: learn-hub's 11 project skills in .claude/skills (atomize-book, ingest-*, sync-vault, ...) can't be plugin-eval'd as they stand. claims.claim: skill-creator's packager excludes a skill-root `evals/` directory from the uploadable .skill bundle, so skill-level evals never ship to claude.ai/API. A plugin-root evals/ travels with the plugin: an installed plugin can be evaluated from its installed copy's eval directory.

claims.implication_for_repo: Keeping skills/<skill>/evals/ is harmless for packaging. Moving cases to plugins/<name>/evals/ lets `claude plugin eval <name>@micky-psych-tools` re-check an installed copy after a marketplace update.

claims.claim: Model and version drift is a reason to re-run evals: a skill that worked last month can behave differently after model or infrastructure changes. For capability-uplift skills, a base model that passes the evals without the skill signals the skill is no longer needed.
claims.quote: If the base model starts passing your evals without the skill loaded, that's a signal the skill's techniques may have been incorporated into the model's default behavior.
claims.implication_for_repo: Re-run each plugin's suite after default-model changes. A persistently ~0 Δ on a long skill's cases is evidence for deleting or shrinking that skill in the rewrite.

open_questions: Does `plugins:` in prompt.md/case.yaml accept several plugin directories so sibling plugins load together (needed to test cross-plugin routing and delegation such as pubmed-research-note -> intent-lock/vault-keeper)? The docs use the plural but show only a single-path example.
`experimental.evals` is typed string|array. With an array (for example one dir per skill), where do results/ go, and are case names deduplicated across dirs? Not documented.

The three MCP-using plugins declare http servers at pubmed.mcp.claude.com and hcls.mcp.claude.com. Would these authenticate inside an isolated eval run with --allow-real-servers, or are mocks the only practical path?

Which field name is canonical for skill-creator checks, `assertions` (SKILL.md, agentskills.io, this repo) or `expectations` (schemas.md, aggregate_benchmark.py)? The viewer and aggregation code read `expectations` in grading.json.

Can `claude plugin eval` be pointed at a marketplace root to run every plugin's suite in one command, or must CI loop over plugins/*? The docs only describe plugin, case-file and installed-plugin targets.

Budget: converting all 118 existing evals at the defaults (3 runs x 2 arms, plus llm-judge calls) is roughly 700 agent runs per full pass. What smoke-subset size and release cadence does the owner accept?

learn-hub/plugins duplicates 4 of micky-psych-tools' evals.json files (intent-lock, misread-capture, comprehensive-review, pubmed-research-note). Should eval suites live only at the source-of-truth copy?

results.evidence: skills.md 'Evaluate and iterate on a skill' says, near-verbatim: '...the skill-creator plugin below runs a similar loop with its own `evals/evals.json` format. The two formats aren't interchangeable.' It also says plugin eval 'exits non-zero below a threshold so you can gate CI on it'. The plugin-evals.md intro repeats the split: 'Its case format is separate from the `evals/evals.json` file the skill-creator plugin uses.'

`claude --version` prints 2.1.280. `claude plugin eval --help` prints the quoted usage line verbatim. plugin-evals.md Requirements says 'Claude Code v2.1.269 or later', and the changelog entry for 2.1.269 (September 11, 2026) is 'Added `claude plugin eval`'.

Verified empirically. I copied plugins/intent-lock to the scratchpad and ran `claude plugin eval <dir> --trust-plugin --ablation none`. It printed 'No eval cases found ... Cases are expected in a evals/ directory ... each case a directory containing case.yaml or prompt.md' and exited 1. No plugin in micky-psych-tools has a plugin-root evals/ dir (`ls plugins/*/evals` finds nothing). All suites live at skills/<skill>/evals/evals.json, and no manifest sets experimental.evals.

Counts check out once the template is excluded. There are 16 evals.json files: 11 real suites in micky-psych-tools, the plugin-creator template (2 placeholder evals), and 4 files in learn-hub/plugins that are byte-identical copies (checked with cmp). Excluding the template that is 15 files and 118 evals. Every eval has exactly the keys {id, name, prompt, expected_output, files, assertions} under a top-level {skill_name, evals}. The overreach is the conversion claim: all 120 `assertions` arrays and all `files` arrays are empty. So no assertion strings exist to turn into graders/*.md, and `context.add_dirs` takes directories, not file paths. Negatives such as 'negative-scaffolding-request-plugin-creator-territory' expect routing to another plugin, and that can't be observed because a run loads only the target plugin (plugin-evals.md, 'How runs are isolated').
results.corrected_claim: Only the skeleton converts mechanically. Mapping: `name` → a case dir (grouped under a non-case dir such as evals/<skill>/<name>/), `prompt` → the prompt.md body, and `expected_output` → the human-only `expected_outcome` field (never scored). Graders cannot be generated mechanically, because every assertions[] is empty. Each case needs hand-authored graders, e.g. an llm rubric distilled from expected_output plus a `tool_used: Skill` grader whose input_match allows the optional `plugin:` prefix. For negative cases, the only possible check is `tool_used: Skill` with min 0 / max 0 / arm: both on this plugin's skill; a positive 'routed to <other plugin>' check is impossible in an isolated run. `files` would need to become a fixture directory (add_dirs) or a scaffold_script. The count is 15 files and 118 evals excluding the plugin-creator template, or 16 and 120 including it.

results.evidence: The doc says '`prompt.md` frontmatter accepts these fields. An unknown key is an error', and its field table lists `expected_outcome`. Verified empirically: adding `expected_output:` to a bare case's prompt.md gave '✗ ... prompt.md: unknown frontmatter key "expected_output" (expected one of: schema_version, name, description, tags, plugins, runs, expected_outcome, model, max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools, artifact_publish, growthbook_overrides, append_system_prompt, env)' and exit 1.

plugin-evals.md: 'To group cases, nest them under a directory that isn't itself a case'. `--case <glob>` and `--tag` filters are documented. For `experimental.evals` the doc says: 'Give a relative path of plain directory names... An absolute path or one containing `..` isn't accepted: as a flag value it's an error, while an unusable manifest value prints a `Warning:` line and the run uses `evals/` instead.' plugins-reference lists `experimental.evals` as string|array.

Verified. Running `claude plugin eval init --bare first-case` in a scratch copy of intent-lock printed 'Created evals/first-case/prompt.md and evals/first-case/graders/criteria.md'. prompt.md held `max_turns: 10` and `allowed_tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]`; criteria.md held `type: llm` and `weight: 1`. The `init --help` text matches the quote. The docs describe the interview and add: 'claude plugin eval init needs a terminal to ask you its questions; in CI, run `claude plugin eval init --bare <name>`'.

The doc says: 'Of the six types, `regex`, `tool_used`, `tool_order`, and `file_exists` are computed from the transcript and files and cost nothing, while `llm` and `baseline` call a judge model... There are no custom-code graders.'
The quote appears verbatim under 'Choose graders that give a stable signal'.

The doc says, verbatim: 'Give each case one grader on the result... and one on how Claude got there, such as `tool_used` or `tool_order`. Together they tell you both whether the answer was right and whether your plugin produced it.'

The doc says: 'For long output such as a generated file, grade it with a `regex` grader... Keep `llm` graders for short outputs'. The grader table says llm passes when 'A judge model votes PASS... in at least two of three votes'. `--help` shows '--judge-model <model> Override LLM-grader model (default: haiku)'.

The 'What a grader can look at' table lists last_message (the default), trace ('A `regex` grader sees every message; an `llm` judge sees the first 12 and the last 12... a regex matches `\"` rather than `"`'), files (paths only), {source: file, path} and mock_calls.

The quote appears verbatim in the target table. The files row reads: 'Not their contents, and not files that a scaffold created or that Claude only modified.' Troubleshooting adds: '`file_exists` counts only files created during the run'.

The doc says: 'If a case scores 1.0 both with and without the plugin, the plugin isn't what made it pass.' It also says: 'Pass `--ablation none` to run only the with-arm, which halves the cost'. Two arms is the default only 'when a plugin resolves'.

The doc lists as excluded 'Every `tool_used` grader whose `tool` is `Skill`' and 'Any grader you mark `arm: with-only`'. It continues: 'If every grader in a case is one of these, they're scored normally instead... Set `arm: both`... for a "must not invoke the skill" check with `min: 0` and `max: 0`.'

The quoted sentence describes the doc's example grader, whose regex builds in an optional namespace prefix: `input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?your-skill-name"'`. Namespaced invocations are matched because of that `(?:[\w-]+:)?` group, not automatically. A regex that only names the bare skill would miss 'plugin:skill'.
results.corrected_claim: The canonical trigger check is a `tool_used` grader on `Skill` with an input_match regex naming the skill. It counts the namespaced `plugin-name:skill-name` form only if the regex allows an optional prefix, as the doc's example does: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?<skill-name>"'. Any converter must emit that form.

results.evidence: The quickstart says: 'The most common first finding is a `Δ` near zero with the case's `tool_used: Skill` grader failing... Adjust the skill's description'. The stable-signal bullets say: 'If a case's `tool_used: Skill` grader passes but `Δ` is negative, suspect the judge before the plugin... Re-run with `--judge-model sonnet`, and tighten the rubric'.

The doc says: 'each case runs three times by default. A run's score is the fraction of its graders that passed, weighted... the case's score is the mean across its runs'. The runs field allows '1 to 50'. The quoted threshold sentence appears verbatim in Troubleshooting. The threshold is compared against the with-arm score.

'How runs are isolated' says each run gets 'a throwaway home directory, working directory, and Claude Code configuration... with only your plugin loaded'. It continues: 'Nothing personal or project-level loads. Your user settings, hooks, `CLAUDE.md` files, MCP servers, other installed plugins, memory, and skills are absent, and no project-scoped `.claude/` or `.mcp.json` above the sandbox is read.'

The prompt.md table has the row `plugins` | 'The nearest enclosing plugin' | 'Plugin directories under test, relative to the case directory. Set `plugins: ["../.."]` when auto-detection doesn't find your plugin'. Only that single-path example is shown.

The table rows are `max_turns` default 10, 'Turn cap, up to 200. Hitting it is recorded as a run error and usually lowers the score, so set it generously', and `timeout_seconds` default 300, 'up to 3600'.

The doc says: 'The allowlist is the read-only tools the case lists in `allowed_tools`, from `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `NotebookRead`, `Skill`, `Agent`, `TodoWrite`, and the task tools TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskList/TaskUpdate/TaskStop, plus whatever you grant with `--allow-tools`. That grant applies to every case in the run.' On Bash it says: 'your home directory and Claude Code configuration are unreadable, and network access is limited'. On the environment: only an allowlist and EVAL_* vars reach the run.

The quoted sentence is verbatim. The doc also says '`@path` mentions in it aren't expanded'. The case.yaml table documents add_dirs ('granted read-only'), scaffold_script (runs 'outside the agent's sandbox, and only when you pass `--scaffold`') and history_file ('the case's prompt becomes the next user turn').

The doc says 'A run never starts your plugin's real MCP servers unless you ask', and the quote on mock files is verbatim. It covers the expect: guard ('the run aborts with score 0'), `type: agent` answering via the judge model, adopting recordings into `.replay/<server>/` ('Commit `mocks/.replay/`... so CI runs are repeatable'), and `_tools.json` holding 'real descriptions and input schemas'. Relevant here: pubmed-research-note, comprehensive-review and psych-paper-digest declare pubmed/clinical-trials servers in .mcp.json, so mocks can be used for them.

The CI example uses exactly those flags. The exit-code table: 0 = all pass; 1 = below threshold / load failure / no cases / run couldn't start / untrusted / invalid option; 2 = partial (cost ceiling or credential rejected); 130 = interrupted; 143 = terminated. On `--model` the doc says 'Pin it in CI so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression'.

The results layout, the `.gitignore` note, `schemaVersion: 1` with camelCase fields (aggregates.overallScore, casesPassed, meanDelta, cases[].aggregates.delta, partial) and 'The Artifact tool is off' are all verbatim. The publish claim overstates the default. The doc publishes only 'If you're signed in with a claude.ai subscription and artifacts are available for your account'. It also says 'A run that a Claude Code session started, such as when you ask Claude to run the suite for you, also stays local... Add `--publish-report`'. For a named installed-plugin target, results go to ./evals/results/ in the current directory.
results.corrected_claim: Each path-target run writes <eval dir>/results/<timestamp>/{aggregate-result.json, report.html}; gitignore results/. A terminal run on a claude.ai subscription with artifacts enabled publishes the report as a private artifact unless --no-publish is passed. API-key runs stay local, and runs started by a Claude Code session stay local unless --publish-report is passed. The Artifact tool is off inside runs.

results.evidence: The doc says: 'a suite makes roughly cases × runs agent runs with the plugin and as many again for the no-plugin baseline, plus three short judge calls per `llm` or `baseline` grader per run'. The quickstart recipe is `--case <name> --runs 1 --ablation none`. The CI section quote is verbatim.

schemas.md shows evals[] with `expectations` ('List of verifiable statements'), and aggregate_benchmark.py reads grading.get("expectations"). skill-creator SKILL.md says 'including the `assertions` field', and eval_metadata.json uses 'assertions'. In the repos, a JSON scan shows 0 of 120 evals (16 files, including the plugin-creator template) with non-empty assertions or files. validate.py lines 111-114 only `json.load` the file. There are no *-workspace dirs and no grading.json, benchmark.json, feedback.json or eval_metadata.json anywhere. That shows no eval was ever graded with assertions. It doesn't prove none was ever run, because skill-creator workspaces are sibling dirs that may never have been kept.
results.corrected_claim: All 118 real evals (120 counting the plugin-creator template, which stamps the same empty pattern into every new plugin) have `assertions: []` and `files: []`, and validate.py only checks that evals.json parses. No grading, benchmark or feedback artifacts exist in either repo, so no eval has demonstrably been graded. Whether any was informally run cannot be established.

The SKILL.md line 394 quote is verbatim. run_loop.py defaults are holdout 0.4, runs-per-query 3, trigger-threshold 0.5 and max-iterations 5. improve_description receives train_results and a history with test_* keys stripped ('blinded_history'). best is chosen by max test_passed. The per-query timeout defaults to 30 s.

It writes a `<skill>-skill-<uuid>.md` command file under the project's .claude/commands/ and runs `claude -p` in the project root with the user's own environment (only CLAUDECODE is stripped). So the user's other skills and plugins stay loaded. A caveat that adds to the claim: it counts a trigger only if the first tool call is Skill/Read on that temp command. If the real installed skill fires instead, that counts as a miss.

When the listing overflows, Claude Code drops descriptions starting with the skills you invoke least', and 'each entry's combined text is capped at 1,536 characters' (configurable via skillListingBudgetFraction / skillListingMaxDescChars). Ran `claude plugin validate .` on micky-psych-tools and on plugins/intent-lock: both passed.

The best-practices page says 'Create evaluations BEFORE writing extensive documentation.' Its five steps: identify gaps without a Skill → 'Build three scenarios' → establish baseline → 'Write minimal instructions' → iterate. The checklist includes '[ ] At least three evaluations created' and '[ ] Tested with Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus'.
