Empirically, CLI 2.1.280 also accepts a bare skill folder (SKILL.md, no manifest). `claude plugin eval .` printed 'Plugin under test: "foo" (no version)' and set up two ablation arms, and `init --bare c1` scaffolded evals/ there. The init error text says 'not a plugin or skill folder'. So 'not a valid target' is false in practice, though it matches the docs.
results.corrected_claim: Documented targets are plugin dirs with a manifest and skills-directory plugins (<name>@skills-dir). CLI 2.1.280 also resolves a bare skill folder (SKILL.md, no manifest) as an unversioned plugin and can run evals for it, but this is undocumented and shouldn't be relied on. For plain .claude/skills skills, the documented route is skill-creator or manual fresh-session with/without comparisons. Every plugin in this repo has a manifest, so this doesn't block anything.

results.evidence: package_skill.py has `ROOT_EXCLUDE_DIRS = {"evals"}` ('Directories excluded only at the skill root'), so evals/ is left out of the .skill zip built for upload. 'Never ship' overreaches. That applies only to package_skill.py bundles. A skill-level evals/ inside a Claude Code plugin is part of the plugin directory and is distributed to anyone who installs the plugin; it is just not runnable by `claude plugin eval`. The installed-copy half is confirmed ('An installed plugin by name... The cases in the installed copy's eval directory').
results.corrected_claim: skill-creator's package_skill.py excludes a skill-root evals/ from the .skill bundle uploaded to claude.ai. Inside a plugin, skills/<skill>/evals/ still ships with the plugin, but `claude plugin eval` never reads it. A plugin-root evals/ (or experimental.evals dir) travels with the plugin, and `claude plugin eval <name>` runs the installed copy's cases, writing results under ./evals/results/ in the current directory.

results.evidence: The blog post (March 3, 2026) says: 'As models and the infrastructure around them evolve, a skill that worked well last month might behave differently today' and 'If the base model starts passing your evals without the skill loaded, that's a signal the skill's techniques may have been incorporated into the model's default behavior.' It says this in the context of capability-uplift skills.

missed_practices.claim: Match the eval goal to the skill type. For capability-uplift skills, evals detect when the base model has caught up. For encoded-preference (workflow) skills, which is most of this repo (intent-lock, vault-keeper, plan-critique, decision-interview), evals should verify fidelity to the owner's actual workflow, so graders belong on process order and hand-offs, not just the final answer.
missed_practices.quote: Capability uplift skills may become less necessary as models improve. Evals tell you when that's happened. Encoded preference skills are more durable, but only as valuable as their fidelity to your actual workflow. Evals verify that fidelity.

missed_practices.claim: Evaluate progressive disclosure by watching which bundled files Claude reads. Unread reference files, repeated reads and unexpected read orders are signals to restructure the skill. In plugin eval this can be graded with `tool_used`/`tool_order` on Read with an input_match naming the reference file. It matters for this repo's reference-heavy skills.
missed_practices.quote: Ignored content: If Claude never accesses a bundled file, it might be unnecessary or poorly signaled in the main instructions

missed_practices.claim: Complement synthetic evals with observation in real workflows: one Claude instance authors or refines the skill ('Claude A') while a fresh instance ('Claude B') uses it on actual tasks, and observed failures feed back into the skill.
missed_practices.quote: Use the Skill in real workflows: Give Claude B (with the Skill loaded) actual tasks, not test scenarios

missed_practices.claim: Close the loop by giving failed assertions, human feedback, execution transcripts and the current SKILL.md to an LLM to propose edits. Instruct it to generalize rather than patch for the test cases, keep the skill lean, explain the why, and bundle repeated helper work into scripts/. This avoids overfitting a small suite.
missed_practices.quote: Generalize from feedback. The skill will be used across many different prompts, not just the test cases. Fixes should address underlying issues broadly rather than adding narrow patches for specific examples.

missed_practices.claim: Define explicit stopping criteria for the iterate loop rather than iterating indefinitely.
missed_practices.quote: Stop when you're satisfied with the results, feedback is consistently empty, or you're no longer seeing meaningful improvement between iterations.

missed_practices.claim: Before reading a score drop as a regression, check run errors for usage- or rate-limit messages. Limit-hit runs score about 0 but the suite is not marked partial.
missed_practices.quote: The suite still finishes and isn't marked `partial`, so the result can look like a regression. Check the `NOTES` column or `cases[].arms.with[].error` in the JSON for the limit message before trusting the scores

missed_practices.claim: A passing eval suite is not a safety vetting. If the plugin ships hooks or runs real MCP servers, treat scores as advisory unless the suite ran in an isolated container or CI runner, because hooks and servers run outside the agent sandbox and can touch the files graders read.
missed_practices.quote: When the plugin ships hooks you didn't write, or you start its real MCP servers, treat its scores as advisory unless you ran it in an isolated environment such as a container or CI runner

missed_practices.claim: Mine the discriminating assertions, the ones that pass with the skill and fail without, to learn which instructions or scripts carry the value. Treat stddev as meaningful only once each eval runs multiple times.
missed_practices.quote: Study assertions that pass with the skill but fail without. This is where the skill is clearly adding value. Understand why — which instructions or scripts made the difference?

research.dimension: COM — community and exemplar practice (anthropics/skills, obra/superpowers, Anthropic engineering/Claude Code blog posts, Simon Willison, Jesse Vincent), with conflicts against official docs flagged

claims.claim: Superpowers' writing-skills rule: the description should state ONLY triggering conditions (start with 'Use when...') and must never summarize the skill's process/workflow, because agents follow the short description as a shortcut and skip the body.
claims.quote: Testing revealed that when a description summarizes the skill's workflow, an agent may follow the description instead of reading the full skill content.
claims.implication_for_repo: Most repo descriptions (e.g. pubmed-research-note 'a quantified, adjudicated evidence report with a clearly marked verdict...') are workflow summaries; rewrite them to trigger conditions + near-miss boundaries and move the procedure summary into the body.

claims.claim: Jesse Vincent reports that from Opus 4.5 onward Claude more often 'winged' a skill it claimed to use, which he attributed to descriptions explaining what the skill does; he rewrote descriptions to contain only when-to-use information.
claims.quote: Starting with Opus 4.5, Claude seemed somewhat more likely to guess that it already knew what a skill did based on the description.
claims.implication_for_repo: Long 'what-it-does' descriptions near the 1024 cap risk Claude acting from the description alone; test the repo's gate skills (intent-lock, decision-interview) for 'announced but not read' behaviour in transcripts.

claims.claim: Anthropic's Claude Code team (Jun 2026) says the description is scanned from the session skill listing to decide whether a skill exists for the request, so it should describe when to trigger, not summarize; include literal trigger words.
claims.quote: Which means the description field is not a summary, it's a description of when to trigger this skill.
claims.implication_for_repo: Converge with COM-01: descriptions should lead with user phrasings/situations (e.g. 'critique this plan', '/digest'), not a feature inventory.

claims.claim: CONFLICT: the official authoring best-practices page and the official skill-creator skill both say the description must include BOTH what the skill does and when to use it, which contradicts the trigger-only rule of superpowers (COM-01) and Anthropic's own Jun-2026 blog (COM-03). The official docs page was fetched today (live); the blog is dated 2026-06-03; superpowers v4 rule dates 2025-12-17. A defensible reconciliation: one short 'what' clause (capability noun phrase, no steps) + trigger conditions, never a workflow sequence.
claims.quote: The `description` field enables Skill discovery and should include both what the Skill does and when to use it.
claims.implication_for_repo: The plan must pick a house rule and encode it in validate.py/plugin-creator templates; recommend 'one-clause capability + triggers + NOT-for boundaries, no step sequence' and verify with trigger evals rather than by argument.

claims.claim: anthropics/skills' skill-creator says Claude tends to undertrigger skills and recommends making descriptions a little 'pushy' (e.g. 'Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions ... even if they don't explicitly ask').
claims.quote: To combat this, please make the skill descriptions a little bit "pushy".
claims.implication_for_repo: Pushiness must be balanced against overlap among sibling skills (comprehensive-review vs pubmed-research-note vs psych-paper-digest); only trigger evals with near-miss negatives can calibrate it.

claims.claim: Exemplar descriptions in anthropics/skills state explicit negative boundaries inside the description (docx: 'Do NOT use for PDFs...'; claude-api uses a TRIGGER/SKIP structure with an explicit SKIP clause that overrides triggers).
claims.quote: Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
claims.implication_for_repo: Keep the repo's 'NOT for ... (use X)' routing boundaries, but put them in the description itself (short) so sibling-skill disambiguation happens at listing time rather than depending on ROUTING.md.

claims.claim: CONFLICT on voice: the Agent Skills open-standard guide says frame the description imperatively ('Use this skill when...'), while the official Anthropic best-practices page says always write in third person and avoid second person ('You can use this to...'). Superpowers mixes both: third person but starting 'Use when...'.
claims.quote: Frame the description as an instruction to the agent: "Use this skill when..." rather than "This skill does..."
claims.implication_for_repo: Pick one voice and lint it; 'Use when <situation>...' (superpowers form) satisfies both the imperative-trigger advice and avoids first/second person pronouns flagged by the official page.

claims.claim: Jesse Vincent reports users hitting Claude Code's hidden character limits on skill descriptions, causing skills to be hidden; he responded by consolidating skills. The current Claude Code docs confirm a listing budget of 1% of the context window that shortens/drops descriptions, starting with least-invoked skills.
claims.quote: some folks have started to run into Claude Code's hidden limits on the number of characters of skill descriptions that are allowed before Claude starts hiding some skills.
claims.implication_for_repo: With ~17 marketplace skills at ~700-1024 chars plus learn-hub's 11 project skills, total descriptions can crowd the listing; run /doctor and /skill-doctor and shorten descriptions rather than rely on the 1024 cap.

claims.claim: Claude Code truncates the combined description + when_to_use text at 1,536 characters in the skill listing and advises putting the key use case first; the listing budget scales at 1% of context and can be raised via skillListingBudgetFraction or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET.
claims.quote: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's '1024 hard cap' is the spec limit, but the effective lever is front-loading: validate.py should also check that the first ~150 chars carry the primary trigger.

claims.claim: CONFLICT on body length: superpowers targets <500 WORDS for ordinary skills (<150-200 for always-loaded ones) and <500 characters for descriptions, whereas the Agent Skills spec and official docs allow up to 500 LINES / <5000 tokens for the SKILL.md body.
claims.quote: - Other skills: <500 words (still be concise)
claims.implication_for_repo: Repo SKILL.md bodies run 600-4,300 words (intent-lock 4,317 words); the official 500-line ceiling is met but the community word target is exceeded 3-8x — the plan should set a word budget (e.g. body <=1,500 words, overflow to references/).

claims.claim: The Agent Skills spec says keep SKILL.md under 500 lines and move detail to separate files; skill-creator treats these numbers as approximate, and an official exemplar (claude-api SKILL.md, 572 lines) exceeds it.
claims.quote: Keep your main `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. Move detailed reference material to separate files.
claims.implication_for_repo: Treat 500 lines as a validate.py warning not an error; the stronger constraint is words-per-activation (COM-10).

claims.claim: Progressive-disclosure pointers should say WHEN to load each reference file (a concrete condition), not just list the references directory.
claims.quote: "Read `references/api-errors.md` if the API returns a non-200 status code" is more useful than a generic "see references/ for details."
claims.implication_for_repo: Audit each SKILL.md's references/ pointers (e.g. plugin-creator, clinical-infographic fidelity contract) and rewrite them as 'Read X when Y' lines; a validate.py check can flag references/ files never named in SKILL.md.

claims.claim: Exemplar practice: bundled scripts are run as black boxes via --help rather than read into context (webapp-testing), and command flags are left to --help rather than documented in SKILL.md (superpowers; Simon Willison makes the same argument for CLI tools).
claims.quote: They exist to be called directly as black-box scripts rather than ingested into your context window.
claims.implication_for_repo: Where repo skills describe scripts' flags in prose (vault-keeper, psych-paper-digest sweeps), give the scripts a good --help and replace the prose with one invocation line.

claims.claim: skill-creator's rule for when to bundle a script: if test-run transcripts show subagents independently writing the same helper, bundle it in scripts/ and tell the skill to use it.
claims.quote: If all 3 test cases resulted in the subagent writing a `create_docx.py` or a `build_chart.py`, that's a strong signal the skill should bundle that script.
claims.implication_for_repo: Use eval transcripts to decide which prose procedures (e.g. PubMed query assembly, HTML self-containment checks in concept-animation/ml-concept-lab) should become scripts.

claims.claim: Exemplars ship validators whose error output names the fix (pptx validate.py), so the model can loop validate-fix without reading validator source; Simon Willison highlights the slack-gif-creator's size-check function for the same self-correction loop.
claims.quote: Schema, relationship, content-type, chart and slide checks; each failure names its fix.
claims.implication_for_repo: Skills producing self-contained HTML (clinical-infographic, concept-animation, code-explainer, ml-concept-lab) should ship a checker script with fix-naming errors instead of long prose contracts.

claims.claim: Superpowers says not to spend skill prose on mechanical constraints that can be enforced by regex/validation — automate them and reserve documentation for judgment calls.
claims.quote: - Mechanical constraints (if it's enforceable with regex/validation, automate it—save documentation for judgment calls)
claims.implication_for_repo: Rules like kebab-case names, version parity, description caps, reduced-motion blocks and 'no external refs' belong in validate.py / bundled checkers, and can be deleted from SKILL.md bodies.

claims.claim: Newer exemplar docx/pptx skills are written as gotchas-only: they assume the model knows the library and list only footguns plus a task->approach table.
claims.quote: The model knows the API; these are the footguns:
claims.implication_for_repo: The firecrawl skill (Firecrawl's onboarding guide kept verbatim, 384 lines) is the opposite pattern; reduce it to a routing table + repo-specific gotchas and push vendor text to references/.

claims.claim: Anthropic's Claude Code team calls the Gotchas section the highest-signal content in a skill, built from observed failure points and updated over time; best skills start as a few lines and a single gotcha.
claims.quote: The highest-signal content in any skill is the Gotchas section.
claims.implication_for_repo: Each rewritten SKILL.md should have an explicit Gotchas section harvested from misread-capture logs and past corrections, instead of diffusing lessons through prose.

claims.claim: Don't state the obvious: content restating default Claude behaviour costs context without value; skills should push Claude out of its normal way of thinking.
claims.quote: A skill that restates what Claude would do by default adds context without adding value.
claims.implication_for_repo: Run a 'would Claude do this anyway?' pass over each skill; generic research-method or HTML-authoring advice is a deletion candidate, domain-specific clinical fidelity rules are not.

claims.claim: Anthropic (Jul 2026) found it had been overconstraining Claude via system prompt, CLAUDE.md and skills; it removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt for Claude 5-generation models with no measurable eval loss, and now advises skills avoid overconstraint except in highly important areas.
claims.quote: We removed over 80% of Claude Code’s system prompt for models like Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5 with no measurable loss on our coding evaluations.
claims.implication_for_repo: This is the newest guidance: default to goal + constraints + gotchas, and reserve hard rules for the genuinely high-stakes gates (clinical fact fidelity, destructive vault deletes).

claims.claim: Avoid railroading: state the goal and constraints rather than every step, because skills are reused across many situations.
claims.quote: Give Claude the information it needs, but give it the flexibility to adapt to the situation.
claims.implication_for_repo: Long fixed step lists (e.g. plan-critique's nine-lens pipeline, intent-lock's interrogation) should be reviewed for which steps are true invariants vs. defaults Claude can adapt.

claims.claim: Superpowers' 'Match the Form to the Failure': prohibitions + rationalization tables are only for discipline failures (agent knows the rule but skips it under pressure); wrong-shaped output needs a positive recipe/contract, omitted elements need a required template slot, and conditional behaviour needs a predicate — prohibitions measurably backfire on shaping problems, and nuance/exemption clauses degrade them.
claims.quote: The form that bulletproofs one failure type measurably backfires on another.
claims.implication_for_repo: Classify each 'never/always' rule in the repo's skills by failure type; e.g. report-shape rules in pubmed-research-note/comprehensive-review should become output contracts, not prohibition lists.

claims.claim: For discipline-enforcing skills, superpowers closes loopholes explicitly: a rationalization table built from verbatim baseline excuses, a 'Red Flags - STOP' list, and an early foundational line that the letter of the rule is its spirit.
claims.quote: **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
claims.implication_for_repo: Appropriate only for the repo's gate skills (intent-lock Step 0, vault-keeper's move->verify->delete order); the tables must come from observed baseline excuses, not invented ones.

claims.claim: Superpowers' persuasion-principles guide scopes emphasis by skill type: heavy authority/commitment language only for discipline skills, moderate for technique skills, and 'clarity only' (no persuasion) for reference skills.
claims.quote: | Reference | Clarity only | All persuasion |
claims.implication_for_repo: Gives a checkable rubric: reference-type content (firecrawl, design systems, lens catalogs) should carry no MUST/NEVER capitals.

claims.claim: CONFLICT on emphatic wording: skill-creator treats all-caps ALWAYS/NEVER and rigid structures as a yellow flag (explain the why instead); the official best-practices page suggests switching to stronger language like 'MUST filter'; superpowers uses 'YOU MUST'/EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT for discipline skills. Newest Anthropic guidance (Jul 2026, COM-20) sides with less constraint.
claims.quote: If you find yourself writing ALWAYS or NEVER in all caps, or using super rigid structures, that's a yellow flag
claims.implication_for_repo: Adopt 'explain the why by default; caps only where a micro-test shows the softer wording fails' and add a validate.py warning counting all-caps MUST/NEVER per skill.

claims.claim: CONFLICT on examples: Anthropic's Sep-2025 context-engineering post strongly advises curated few-shot examples, superpowers says one excellent example beats many; Anthropic's Jul-2026 post (newer) reports that examples constrain Claude 5-generation models and recommends expressive interface design instead.
claims.quote: With our newest models, we’ve found that giving examples actually constrains them to a certain exploration space.
claims.implication_for_repo: Worked examples under examples/ (ml-concept-lab, code-explainer template) should be framed as references loaded on demand, not inline few-shot in SKILL.md; test whether they narrow output variety.

claims.claim: Superpowers treats skill writing as TDD: run a baseline scenario with a subagent WITHOUT the skill, record failures verbatim, write the minimal skill addressing them, re-run WITH it, then close loopholes; this applies to edits too.
claims.quote: **Core principle:** If you didn't watch an agent fail without the skill, you don't know if the skill teaches the right thing.
claims.implication_for_repo: Each rewrite should start by running the existing evals/evals.json prompts against a no-skill baseline to prove which instructions actually change behaviour before cutting or adding.

claims.claim: Jesse Vincent found that subagent 'tests' posed as quizzes gave false perfect scores; realistic pressure scenarios that force a concrete choice (combining 3+ pressures like time, sunk cost, authority) were what exposed violations.
claims.quote: I discovered that Claude was quizzing the subagents like they were on a gameshow. This was less than useful.
claims.implication_for_repo: Gate skills (intent-lock, decision-interview, vault-keeper empty-vault) need pressure-scenario evals (e.g. 'user is in a hurry, skip the interview'), not just happy-path prompts.

claims.claim: Before full scenarios, superpowers micro-tests wording: fresh-context single samples, a mandatory no-guidance control (if the control doesn't fail, don't write the guidance), 5+ reps per variant, and manual reading of every flagged match.
claims.quote: 2. **Always include a no-guidance control.** If the control doesn't exhibit the failure, there is nothing to fix — stop, don't author the guidance.
claims.implication_for_repo: Provides a deletion test for the rewrite: any rule whose no-guidance control already behaves correctly can be cut.

claims.claim: skill-creator runs each eval twice in parallel in the same turn — with the skill and a baseline (no skill for new skills; a snapshot of the old version when improving) — then grades assertions, aggregates a benchmark, and shows a human viewer before revising.
claims.quote: For each test case, spawn two subagents in the same turn — one with the skill, one without.
claims.implication_for_repo: For a rewrite, the baseline is the current plugin version: snapshot each skill before editing and run old_skill vs new_skill on the existing evals.json.

claims.claim: skill-creator's description optimizer uses ~20 realistic queries (8-10 should-trigger, 8-10 should-not), splits 60% train / 40% held-out test, runs each query 3 times for a trigger rate, and selects the best description by held-out score.
claims.quote: It splits the eval set into 60% train and 40% held-out test, evaluates the current description (running each query 3 times to get a reliable trigger rate)
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo has no should_trigger eval sets at all (grep finds none); add a trigger-eval file per skill so description rewrites are measured, not guessed.

claims.claim: The most valuable negative trigger queries are near-misses that share keywords with the skill but need something else; obviously irrelevant negatives test nothing.
claims.quote: For the **should-not-trigger** queries (8-10), the most valuable ones are the near-misses
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's sibling families (comprehensive-review/pubmed-research-note/psych-paper-digest; concept-animation/ml-concept-lab; intent-lock/decision-interview/plan-critique) supply ready-made near-miss negatives for each other.

claims.claim: Trigger evals must use substantive, multi-step queries: Claude only consults skills for tasks it can't easily do alone, so simple one-step prompts won't trigger even a perfectly matching description.
claims.quote: simple, one-step queries like "read this PDF" may not trigger a skill even if the description matches perfectly
claims.implication_for_repo: Write trigger queries with realistic clinical/project context (file paths, drug names, vault topics), not one-liners.

claims.claim: Inconsistency inside skill-creator: SKILL.md refers to an 'assertions' field in evals.json, while references/schemas.md defines the field as 'expectations' (grading.json uses text/passed/evidence).
claims.quote: - `evals[].expectations`: List of verifiable statements
claims.implication_for_repo: All 11 repo evals.json files use 'assertions' (plus a non-schema 'name' key); decide whether to align with schemas.md's 'expectations' and have validate.py enforce one schema.

claims.claim: skill-creator's quick_validate.py (also used by package_skill.py) rejects frontmatter keys outside {name, description, license, allowed-tools, metadata, compatibility} and rejects angle brackets in descriptions; Claude Code docs confirm claude.ai upload/packaging fails hard on non-spec keys (e.g. argument-hint) while Claude Code itself accepts them.
claims.quote: Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)
claims.implication_for_repo: If these skills should also run on claude.ai/Cowork, validate.py needs a 'portable' profile (spec-only keys, no '<'/'>' in descriptions); Claude Code-only keys stay allowed for the CC profile.

claims.claim: Superpowers references other skills by fully-qualified name with explicit requirement markers and forbids @-file links, because @ force-loads the file into context immediately.
claims.quote: **Why no @ links:** `@` syntax force-loads files immediately, consuming 200k+ context before you need them.
claims.implication_for_repo: Delegations (e.g. 'vault writes go through vault-keeper', 'Act items hand off to pubmed-research-note') should be written as 'REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: vault-keeper:vault-keeper' style name references, never @paths.

claims.claim: Anthropic notes skill-to-skill dependency management is not native to marketplaces yet; referencing another skill by name works if it is installed.
claims.quote: you can just reference other skills by name, and the model will invoke them if they are installed.
claims.implication_for_repo: Cross-plugin handoffs (intent-lock gate, vault-keeper, firecrawl engine) need a stated fallback when the dependency plugin is not installed.

claims.claim: Claude Code copies installed plugins to a cache, so a plugin cannot reference files outside its own directory (e.g. ../shared-utils); within-plugin cross-skill relative links (as superpowers does, ../using-superpowers/references/...) still work.
claims.quote: Copied plugins can't reference files outside their directory using paths like `../shared-utils`, because those files won't be copied.
claims.implication_for_repo: Shared contracts (clinical fidelity rules, vault schema) cannot live in a repo-level shared/ folder referenced by path from several plugins; either duplicate with a sync check, or keep them in one plugin and delegate by skill name.

claims.claim: The official exemplar repo chooses duplication for shared code: docx and pptx each carry a byte-identical scripts/office/soffice.py (and validate.py) so each skill stays self-contained.
claims.quote: | `scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf deck.pptx` | LibreOffice wrapper — bare `soffice` hangs in this sandbox |
claims.implication_for_repo: Verified locally: md5 of skills/docx/scripts/office/soffice.py == skills/pptx/scripts/office/soffice.py (2508a6df). If the repo duplicates shared files across plugins, add a validate.py parity check (the learn-hub already uses byte-identical-twin + parity-test for mermaid-split/tag-canon).

claims.claim: Superpowers consolidated several standalone skills into progressively-disclosed parts of broader skills (to save listing budget) and judged a 'what not to do' skill a mistake — skills should be about what to do.
claims.quote: testing-anti-patterns was a bad skill, because it was about what not to do, rather than being about what to do
claims.implication_for_repo: Candidates for merge-into-references: intent-lock's misread-capture, plugin-creator's refine-plugin, vault-keeper's empty-vault — decide by trigger evals whether they need their own listing slot.

claims.claim: Anthropic catalogued its internal skills into nine categories and found the best skills fit cleanly into one; skills straddling several confuse the agent. The open standard similarly warns against both too-narrow and too-broad scope.
claims.quote: The best skills fit cleanly into one; the ones that try to do too much straddle several and confuse the agent.
claims.implication_for_repo: Skills that combine research + authoring + filing (comprehensive-review, clinical-infographic) should keep one job and delegate the rest by name.

claims.claim: Superpowers deprecated (v5.0.0) then removed (v5.1.0, 2026-04-30) its slash commands because they were stubs that only told Claude to invoke the matching skill; earlier it had marked them disable-model-invocation to stop Claude invoking redirect commands. Claude Code docs now state custom commands are merged into skills.
claims.quote: They were deprecated stubs that did nothing but tell the user to invoke the corresponding skill.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's thin commands ('Run the `plan-critique` skill now.') are exactly this pattern; since a skill directory already yields /<name>, consider deleting them or moving argument-hint/$ARGUMENTS handling into the skill frontmatter.

claims.claim: Superpowers routes via a bootstrap skill (using-superpowers) injected by a SessionStart hook on startup|clear|compact, which tells Claude to check skills before any response and sets process-skill-first priority; it also states user instructions (CLAUDE.md) outrank skills.
claims.quote: "matcher": "startup|clear|compact"
claims.implication_for_repo: An alternative to the generated ROUTING.md + /route: a small injected router, or simply better descriptions; any injected router must stay tiny (superpowers targets <150-200 words for always-loaded content).

claims.claim: Naming: superpowers prefers active, verb-first/gerund names that name the action or core insight; the official best-practices page likewise suggests gerund form and warns against vague names like helper/utils.
claims.quote: - ✅ `creating-skills` not `skill-creation`
claims.implication_for_repo: Renames are costly (routing, vault references, installs); treat as optional — the repo's names are already specific (not 'helper'), so keep them unless a rename also fixes a scope problem.

claims.claim: Flowcharts (DOT/ASCII) are for non-obvious decision points and loops where the agent might stop early, not for linear steps or reference; Jesse reports Claude follows DOT process definitions well.
claims.quote: Claude is particularly good at following processes written in dot.
claims.implication_for_repo: Replace long prose routing branches (e.g. intent-lock's decision gate, empty-vault's move->verify->delete) with one small decision graph; keep linear procedures as numbered lists.

claims.claim: Invoke bundled scripts through their interpreter in SKILL.md prose, never by bare path, because some plugin packagers strip executable bits.
claims.quote: Invoke bundled scripts through their interpreter in the prose (`bash scripts/tool.sh`, `node scripts/tool.js`), never by bare path: some harness plugin packagers strip executable bits
claims.implication_for_repo: Add a validate.py lint that flags bare `scripts/...` invocations without python3/node/bash in SKILL.md and commands.

claims.claim: Anthropic recommends persisting skill state/memory under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} (stable dir), storing setup in a config file and asking the user when it is missing, and measuring undertriggering by logging skill usage with a PreToolUse hook; Claude Code also ships /skill-doctor for per-skill cost and usage.
claims.quote: You can use the env variable ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} to get a stable directory where you can store data
claims.implication_for_repo: psych-paper-digest's .psych-paper-digest.json (config + last_swept) is a candidate to move to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}; add usage logging to find which of the 17 skills undertrigger.

claims.claim: The anthropics/skills marketplace defines plugins with strict:false entries that list skill directories from a shared source root and carry no per-plugin version; Claude Code docs say that with strict:false the marketplace entry is the plugin's entire definition, and a version set in either plugin.json or the entry pins updates to that string.
claims.quote: | `false`          | The marketplace entry is the entire definition.
claims.implication_for_repo: The repo's 'version lives in two files' drift hazard can be removed structurally (declare version in exactly one place, or rely on the next version-management source) rather than policed by bump.py.

claims.claim: Read execution transcripts, not only final outputs, to find instructions that cause wasted work; superpowers adds automated tests that skills trigger from naive prompts without naming them.
claims.quote: Make sure to read the transcripts, not just the final outputs
claims.implication_for_repo: The eval loop for the rewrite should capture transcripts (claude -p JSONL) and check both 'skill was loaded' and 'no unproductive steps', as superpowers' tests/skill-triggering does.

open_questions: Trigger-only descriptions (superpowers, Anthropic Jun-2026 blog) vs 'what + when' (official best-practices page, skill-creator): which triggers better on the current model (Opus 5.5) for this repo's overlapping sibling skills? Needs an A/B run of trigger evals per skill.

Does the combined skill listing (micky-psych-tools marketplace + learn-hub .claude/skills + user/anthropic-skills) already exceed the 1%-of-context listing budget so descriptions are being shortened or dropped? Check with /doctor and /skill-doctor in a real session.

Do superpowers' bulletproofing techniques (MUST, rationalization tables) still help on Claude 5-generation models given Anthropic's Jul-2026 finding that removing 80% of constraints cost nothing? Needs micro-tests with a no-guidance control for the repo's gate skills.
Which evals.json assertion key does the current skill-creator grader/aggregator actually read — 'assertions' (SKILL.md prose, used by all repo evals) or 'expectations' (references/schemas.md)?

Should cross-plugin shared contracts (vault format, clinical fidelity rules) be duplicated with a parity check or centralised in one plugin and reached by skill-name delegation, given copied plugins cannot read ../ paths?

Should the repo's thin slash commands be deleted in favour of skills-as-commands (argument-hint, disable-model-invocation in SKILL.md frontmatter), and would that break the generated ROUTING.md / /route workflow?
Are the skills meant to be portable to claude.ai/Cowork? If yes, frontmatter must be restricted to the six spec keys and descriptions must avoid angle brackets.
sources_read: local: /home/user/micky-psych-tools/plugins/*/skills/*/SKILL.md sizes, evals/evals.json keys, commands/*.md, scripts/validate.py

results.evidence: obra/superpowers writing-skills/SKILL.md (raw, fetched 2026-09-23) lines 99-102: "`description`: Third-person, describes ONLY when to use (NOT what it does) - Start with \"Use when...\" ... **NEVER summarize the skill's process or workflow**"; line 154 has the quoted sentence verbatim, plus the two-review example, and line 158: "Descriptions that summarize workflow create a shortcut agents will take. The skill body becomes documentation agents skip."

blog.fsck.com/2025/12/18/superpowers-4 has the quote verbatim, followed by: "claiming it was going to use a skill and then....winging it without actually reading the skill. I believe that this was mostly caused by skill description fields that explain what a skill does, in addition to when to use it ... I revised skill descriptions to contain only information about when to use the skill." Nuance: his own rewritten brainstorming description still ends with a short 'what' clause ("Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation."), and the live SKILL.md keeps it.

claude.com/blog/lessons-from-building-claude-code-how-we-use-skills (Thariq Shihipar, published Jun 03, 2026): "When Claude Code starts a session, it builds a listing of every available skill with its description. This listing is what Claude scans to decide 'is there a skill for this request?' Which means the description field is not a summary, it's a description of when to trigger this skill." The trigger-word advice is its caption: "It's helpful to include triggers for the skill, like 'babysit,' in its description."

The live platform.claude.com best-practices page (line 203) has the quote verbatim, and also says "Include both what the Skill does and specific triggers/contexts for when to use it". The skill-creator SKILL.md line 67 says "include both what the skill does AND specific contexts for when to use it". The live code.claude.com/docs/en/skills frontmatter table also defines description as "What the skill does and when to use it." So the conflict with superpowers and the Jun-2026 blog is real. The proposed reconciliation (one short 'what' clause, no steps) matches superpowers' own current brainstorming description: "...modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation."

skill-creator SKILL.md line 67: "Note: currently Claude has a tendency to \"undertrigger\" skills ... To combat this, please make the skill descriptions a little bit \"pushy\"." The example includes "Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions dashboards... even if they don't explicitly ask for a 'dashboard.'" agentskills.io/skill-creation/optimizing-descriptions agrees: "Err on the side of being pushy."

docx/SKILL.md frontmatter ends: "Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation." The claude-api/SKILL.md description has a "TRIGGER — ... whenever:" line and a "SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers)" line.

agentskills.io optimizing-descriptions line 25: "**Use imperative phrasing.** Frame the description as an instruction to the agent: 'Use this skill when...' rather than 'This skill does...'" The platform best-practices Warning says: "**Always write in third person** ... Avoid: 'I can help you...' Avoid: 'You can use this to process Excel files'". superpowers writing-skills: "`description`: Third-person ... Start with 'Use when...'". Note: an imperative 'Use when' is not literally second person, so the tension is real but narrower than a flat contradiction.

The superpowers-4 post has the quote verbatim; the next line is: "To help mitigate that, I condensed a number of skills that really didn't need to be standalone skills into progressively-disclosed parts of more general skills." code.claude.com/docs/en/skills line 1083: "The budget scales at 1% of the model's context window. When the listing overflows, Claude Code drops descriptions starting with the skills you invoke least, so the skills you use most keep their full text."

code.claude.com/docs/en/skills frontmatter table: "Put the key use case first: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing". missed_practices.claim: For internal plugins under active development, omit `version` from BOTH plugin.json and the marketplace entry, so updates follow the git commit SHA. When both are set, plugin.json wins. This removes the two-file version-drift trap this repo guards with bump.py.
missed_practices.quote: **Commit-SHA version** | Omit `version` from both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry | Users get updates whenever the source's resolved commit changes | Internal or team plugins under active development

missed_practices.claim: Run the built-in `claude plugin validate --strict` in CI or pre-commit. The runtime only warns on unrecognized fields, so without --strict a typo'd or non-spec field ships silently.
missed_practices.quote: `claude plugin validate` reports unrecognized fields as warnings, not errors. (CLI --help: "--strict  Treat warnings as errors (exit 1). Use in CI to fail on unrecognized fields, missing metadata, and other issues that the runtime tolerates.")

missed_practices.claim: Control who invokes each skill. Use `disable-model-invocation: true` for task/workflow skills the user should trigger with /name (optionally `context: fork` to run in a subagent). Use `user-invocable: false` for background-knowledge skills. Now that commands are merged into skills, this replaces separate redirect commands.
missed_practices.quote: Task content gives Claude step-by-step instructions for a specific action, like deployments, commits, or code generation. These are often actions you want to invoke directly with `/skill-name` rather than letting Claude decide when to run them. Add `disable-model-invocation: true` to prevent Claude from triggering it automatically.

missed_practices.claim: Remove 'think carefully' / 'think step by step' lines from saved instructions, including skills and CLAUDE.md. Current models already think before replying, and these lines only add latency.
missed_practices.quote: Remove “think carefully,” “think step by step,” and similar lines from your prompts and your saved instructions. Opus 5.5 always thinks before it replies, and it decides how much.

missed_practices.claim: Provide defaults, not menus. When several approaches could work, name one default and mention alternatives briefly. Presenting equal options causes wasted exploration, which shows up in execution traces.
missed_practices.quote: When multiple tools or approaches could work, pick a default and mention alternatives briefly rather than presenting them as equal options.

missed_practices.claim: Ground skills in real, project-specific expertise, such as hands-on task transcripts, incident reports, runbooks and past outputs. An LLM writing from general knowledge produces generic procedures.
missed_practices.quote: A common pitfall in skill creation is asking an LLM to generate a skill without providing domain-specific context — relying solely on the LLM's general training knowledge. The result is vague, generic procedures ("handle errors appropriately," "follow best practices for authentication") rather than the specific API patterns, edge cases, and project conventions that make a skill valuable.

missed_practices.claim: Invest most in verification skills and verification steps inside skills (scripts, programmatic assertions on state). Internally at Anthropic these had the largest measured effect on output quality.
missed_practices.quote: Verification skills have had the most measurable impact on Claude’s output quality internally. It can be worth having an engineer spend a week just making your verification skills excellent.

missed_practices.claim: Keep references one level deep from SKILL.md. Every reference file should be linked directly from SKILL.md, not chained through other references. Give reference files longer than 100 lines a table of contents so partial reads still show their scope.
missed_practices.quote: **Keep references one level deep from SKILL.md**. All reference files should link directly from SKILL.md to ensure Claude reads complete files when needed.

research.title: Local conventions, history and open items

research.dimension: LOC — the two repos' own plugin conventions, tooling, unfinished plans, and fork/sync state (micky-psych-tools + learn-hub), checked against the installed CLI (Claude Code 2.1.280) and current official docs

claims.claim: micky-psych-tools makes version parity a hard rule: plugin.json version must equal the marketplace entry version. validate.py:81-82 checks it and bump.py:51 writes both files.
claims.quote: A plugin's version in `plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` MUST equal its entry in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
claims.implication_for_repo: The rewrite has to either keep this rule or replace it on purpose. LOC-02/03 show the current docs and CLI now point the other way.

claims.claim: Current official docs tell plugin authors NOT to put version in both plugin.json and the marketplace entry. They say plugin.json always wins. The repo rule forces the dual-write the docs warn against.
claims.quote: Avoid setting `version` in both `plugin.json` and the marketplace entry. Claude Code always uses the `plugin.json` value without warning, so a stale manifest version can mask a version you set in `marketplace.json`.
claims.implication_for_repo: Keep version in plugin.json only, drop it from catalog entries, and retire bump.py's dual-write. The rationale in CLAUDE.md/README ('catalog version compared, silent no-update') is now inverted.

claims.claim: The installed CLI already catches version drift. Test: a scratch copy with the entry set to 0.1.9 and plugin.json at 0.1.0. `claude plugin validate --strict .` warned and exited 1. `claude plugin tag` also validates that the two agree.
claims.source_url: claude plugin validate --strict . (Claude Code 2.1.280, scratch copy with drifted entry)
claims.quote: At install time, plugin.json wins (calculatePluginVersion precedence) — the entry version is silently ignored.
claims.implication_for_repo: validate.py's parity check duplicates native `--strict`. README.md:57 ('The validator enforces things the CLI does not: ... version parity') is stale.

claims.claim: Both validators pass today. validate.py prints 'all checks passed'. `claude plugin validate --strict` passes on the micky marketplace and on each of the 14 plugin dirs.
claims.quote: √ Validation passed
claims.implication_for_repo: The rewrite starts from a mechanically clean baseline. Run `claude plugin validate --strict` alongside or instead of validate.py, and keep only the checks the CLI lacks (e.g. min description length).

claims.claim: validate.py hard-fails any skill description over 1024 chars and any under 200 chars. Both are house numbers: the 200 floor is a heuristic, and 1024 is stricter than the current runtime budget.
claims.quote: check(n <= 1024, f"skills/{skill}: description {n} chars (hard cap 1024)")
claims.implication_for_repo: Re-base the cap on the docs' 1,536 combined description+when_to_use limit (LOC-06), or keep 1024 as a deliberate style cap and label it that way.

claims.claim: Current docs cap the COMBINED description + when_to_use text at 1,536 chars in the skill listing. when_to_use is a separate frontmatter field that no skill in either repo uses. The repos' custom parsers (validate.py/route.py frontmatter()) ignore it.
claims.quote: the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing to reduce context usage.
claims.implication_for_repo: Move the long trigger-phrase lists out of `description` into `when_to_use`, and teach validate.py/route.py to read the field or drop them for the CLI.

claims.quote: skills/plan-critique: description 1012 chars (hard cap 1024)

claims.claim: route.py builds ROUTING.md from the 'Use when' clause of each description, truncated to a 200-char cue. That imposes wording rules on descriptions that exist only for the custom router: exclusions must be phrased 'NOT for:', and boundary words must sit in the first 200 chars. MEMORY records that Thai triggers and decision-interview's mid-task scoping were moved to survive this window.
claims.quote: Matches the FIRST such clause — description authors must phrase exclusions as "NOT for:", never "Do not use when…", or the exclusion becomes the cue.
claims.implication_for_repo: Custom-router constraints are shaping descriptions that Claude Code reads in full. A rewrite should decide whether ROUTING.md is still worth constraining authoring for.

claims.claim: CLAUDE.md orders the agent to consult the generated ROUTING.md (or /route) before acting on any request a plugin could serve. The generator itself admits the table only re-indexes the descriptions Claude already routes on natively.

results.evidence: CLAUDE.md:40-41 has the quote verbatim. validate.py:81-82 checks `entry.get("version") == man.get("version")`. bump.py:50-51 sets `man["version"] = new` and `entry["version"] = new`, then line 53 writes plugin.json and line 54 writes marketplace.json.

The plugin-marketplaces page has a Warning box with the exact quote. plugins-reference agrees in the manifest table: "If also set in the marketplace entry, `plugin.json` wins." The repo rule (CLAUDE.md:40) and bump.py require writing the version in both places.

Reproduced on CLI 2.1.280 with a scratch copy: intent-lock's catalog entry set to 0.1.9 while its plugin.json stays 0.4.2 (not 0.1.0, a trivial difference). `claude plugin validate --strict .` printed "Entry declares version \"0.1.9\" but ... says \"0.4.2\". At install time, plugin.json wins (calculatePluginVersion precedence) — the entry version is silently ignored." and exited 1. Without --strict it only warns and exits 0. `claude plugin tag --help` says: "Create a {name}--v{version} git tag for a plugin release, validating that plugin.json and any enclosing marketplace entry agree".
`python3 scripts/validate.py` printed 'all checks passed'. `claude plugin validate --strict .` on the marketplace, and on each of the 14 plugins/* directories, printed '√ Validation passed'.

validate.py:109-110 hard-fails a description over 1024 chars or under 200 chars. The 200 floor is a house heuristic. 1024 is not purely a house number, though. The Agent Skills spec (agentskills.io/specification) says "Max 1024 characters", and the platform best-practices page says "Maximum 1,024 characters". Only Claude Code's own listing is looser (1,536 combined chars), and `claude plugin validate --strict` accepts descriptions over 1024 (learn-hub's 1,075–1,150-char descriptions pass).
results.corrected_claim: validate.py hard-fails a skill description over 1024 or under 200 chars. The 200 floor is a house heuristic. The 1024 cap matches the Agent Skills open-standard / Claude API limit ('Max 1024 characters'). It is stricter than Claude Code's own listing budget (1,536 chars for description + when_to_use combined), and Claude Code's validator does not enforce it.

results.corrected_claim: route.py builds each ROUTING.md cue from the first 'Use when…' clause of a description. The clause ends at the first '. ' and is truncated to 200 chars. Descriptions must therefore avoid phrasing exclusions as '…use when…', and must put boundary words early in the Use-when clause, before its first sentence break. strengths: Fork banner with date and upstream sha

group_level_observations: Measured description lengths sit at the 1024-char hard cap: comprehensive-review 1020 (99.6%), pubmed-research-note 1007 (98%), psych-paper-digest 939 (92%); forks 991 and 1011. validate.py counts len() chars, so there is no headroom for a routing fix without cutting. In all three, the first ~200 chars carry only WHAT; the trigger phrases (WHEN) start around char 250, and ROUTING.md truncates at ~200. Each spends 70-170 chars on engine lists/output mechanics that belong in the body.

No unit ships a script. Deterministic work is prose: window math, 90-day cap, JSON config read/write, last_swept advance, digest filename collision, DOI/PMID/NCT dedup grep, Sources-line linting (no authors/journal/year/PMID), 'every section has a number'. Several failure conditions police exactly these.

Evals: 34 evals across the 3 upstream skills (17/5/12). All have 'assertions': [] and 'files': [], and there is no should-trigger/should-not-trigger query set for tuning descriptions. Several evals assume uncontrollable world states (PubMed down; a window holding only confirmatory trials). Both forks copied their evals byte-for-byte, so 3 of the forks' evals now fail by construction (vault-keeper handoffs).

All 5 units bundle a byte-identical .mcp.json (md5 1b35ee7c...) with the same two HTTP servers and hardcode plugin-scoped prefixes plus 'no ToolSearch'. Installing all three upstream plugins registers the same servers three times. The instructions also ignore an equivalent claude.ai connector (this session exposes mcp__PubMed__* and mcp__Clinical_Trials__*). A shared engine layer or runtime tool resolution would remove this duplication.

Shared contracts are copy-pasted rather than referenced: depth contract, citation discipline, Sources grammar, firecrawl policy, PubMed fallback. Drift already exists: the NCT Sources-line grammar has 3 variants across the group, and the preface block has 2 variants (Assumed/Reframed/Skipped vs Assumed/Skipped).

Upstream drift against intent-lock 0.4.2, installed in both repos. intent-lock now forbids reframes and says it emits 'no Reframed line' and 'no preface block'. pubmed-research-note still mandates a Reframed line and a 'reframe governs' rule. Eval 13 still expects intent-lock's visible 'cold read / ledger / rounds / gates'.

intent-lock and vault-keeper are mandatory default steps in the two writers, but no unit says what to do when that plugin is not installed. The marketplace installs plugins individually, so nothing guarantees these dependencies are present.

Name collision: an unrelated claude.ai skill, anthropic-skills:psych-paper-digest (a daily 8-12 paper, 10-domain digest), shares the name and trigger vocabulary of this repo's watchlist psych-paper-digest. pubmed-research-note's NOT-for clause describes the claude.ai version.

Forks: `git diff --stat f91b3b0 HEAD` is empty for both upstream dirs, so upstream is frozen at the fork point. The forks changed only the filing path, but each fork copies the whole plugin, including the version, CHANGELOG and evals. The two forks now disagree on the digest gate: pubmed gates the digest on 'atomize', while comprehensive-review digests and syncs to live Supabase by default. digest-report's own description sides with the atomize gate. Upstream vault-keeper's empty-vault already hands artifacts to learn-hub's digest-report, so there are two parallel routes into the same /vault. The per-repo difference could be expressed as a configuration/adapter layer (output sink = vault-keeper | research-notes+digest-report) rather than as forked copies.

Version-history narration is embedded in operational text across the group ('the old version', 'as of this version', 'replaces the old four frames', 'past reviews have run ~20 to 65+'). It costs always-loaded tokens and goes stale.
CHANGELOG gaps: pubmed-research-note lacks 1.3.0 and 1.4.0, and psych-paper-digest lacks 0.1.1. These releases are recorded only in MEMORY.md.

Token budget: pubmed-research-note's always-loaded body is ~4.7k tokens, plus ~5.9k tokens of references it requires reading every run (decision-brief, report-craft, tool-catalog). Progressive disclosure therefore saves little, and much of that load is repetition: the opt-out rule appears 4x and the depth contract 4x.

units.purpose: Mid-task decision gate: sweeps the task for every decision that needs the user, triages by materiality (destructive steps always ask), and resolves them in batched option-picker rounds with a recommended option first. Records a decision ledger that governs the rest of the session; unattended sessions get an autonomous fallback.

It restates the procedure chain (sweep → triage → order → picker interview → decision ledger → resume) in one line; that summary is accurate and does not contradict the skill.

group_level_observations: Boundary carve-outs are reciprocal in the three gate descriptions: intent-lock names decision-interview, plan-critique and misread-capture; decision-interview names intent-lock, misread-capture and plan-critique; plan-critique names intent-lock ×2 and decision-interview. But the discriminators are session STATES (is the goal locked? does a plan artifact exist? was work delivered?), not phrases, and phrase-level collisions remain. (a) At task start, 'ask me everything at once' / 'what do you need from me' (decision-interview) and 'ask me until you understand' (intent-lock) both match; decision-interview relies only on the word 'mid-task' to disambiguate. (b) 'review my plan' (plan-critique) collides with misread-ledger Active prior #1 ('review' → run intent-lock first). (c) plan-critique routes plan drafting to intent-lock, but intent-lock's description has no drafting trigger and excludes 'already-precise requests'. (d) misread-capture's Not-for carves out only intent-lock mid-interview corrections; plan-critique has no misread-capture carve-out.

ROUTING.md, which CLAUDE.md makes the mandatory first stop, cannot see any Not-for clause: route.py:54-75 builds the cue from the 'Use when' clause truncated at 200 chars. decision-interview's boundary survives only because 'mid-task' was front-loaded into its Use-when clause (MEMORY.md 2026-07-28). intent-lock's row (ROUTING.md:12) loses its unprompted-offer condition, its Not-for and its second Thai trigger.

Family vocabulary has drifted where behavior is meant to be shared. Silence: intent-lock:190 'Silence is a stop', decision-interview:81 'silence is a stop, not a license to wait', plan-critique:50 'silence and an abandoned picker are not a stop verdict'. Question cap: 3 (intent-lock) vs 4 (decision-interview, plan-critique). Picker type names: `single_select`/`multi_select`/`rank_priorities` (intent-lock) vs 'multiSelect' (the siblings). 'Ledger' names four different things: the misread file, intent-lock's [OPEN]/[RESOLVED] item list, decision-interview's [ASK]/[DEFAULT] sweep, and the printed Decided/Defaults block. Surfacing lines differ: 'Assumed: … — say if wrong' vs 'Decided: … / Defaults: …' vs 'Decided without you:'. Recommended-first (decision-interview, plan-critique) vs no-recommendation with a mandatory escape (intent-lock) is deliberate and worth keeping, but it should be stated once as a family rule.

Shared mechanics are copy-pasted three times with small wording drift: the admission threshold ('materially different work … more than roughly a fifth'), the destructive/irreversible/outward-facing always-ask, the autonomous fallback, picker mechanics, stop sovereignty, push-once, and the two-empty-rounds guard. Plugins cannot reference files outside their own directory, so a shared reference is impossible without merging the gates into one plugin (e.g. one 'alignment' plugin with intent-lock, decision-interview, plan-critique and misread-capture skills plus a shared references/interview-contract.md), or without a parity-check script.

None of the three gates names Claude Code's actual picker tool (AskUserQuestion: 1–4 questions, 2–4 options, `multiSelect`, automatic 'Other'). intent-lock is written against the claude.ai tool: `rank_priorities` does not exist, and its manual escape duplicates the automatic 'Other'. All three forbid prose questions, yet the picker is absent in subagents (this workflow agent's tool list has no AskUserQuestion) and headless runs, and it failed in remote sessions (MEMORY.md: 'transport error', 'permission stream closed', 'no interactive intent-lock available'). decision-interview and plan-critique at least have an autonomous fallback; intent-lock has none, and its 'silence/abandoned picker' stop is not observable in Claude Code.

The 'mandatory Step 0 intent-lock' cannot be guaranteed to execute. It is mandatory with failure conditions in pubmed-research-note (SKILL.md:310), comprehensive-review (:209), concept-animation (:168), ml-concept-lab (:241) and firecrawl Path C (:359-361), and in learn-hub's pubmed/comprehensive clones. Yet: no plugin.json declares the dependency; micky-psych-tools has no .claude/ settings and learn-hub's settings.json enables no plugins; intent-lock is absent from this cloud session's available-skills list; and no caller documents a not-installed fallback — only learn-hub pk-plasma-animation:34 says 'if it is available', and MEMORY.md shows sessions improvising one. Even when installed, three things break the contract. The picker may be unavailable. The handoff interface has drifted: callers print 'Reframed:'/'Skipped:', which intent-lock 0.3.0 abolished. And intent-lock has no notion of being a callee (it 'produces no artifact' and its outputs such as GOAL UNIFIED and [ASSUMED] are internal-only), while callers depend on four specific slots being 'closed at GOAL UNIFIED'. learn-hub's concept-animation instead inlines a small caller-owned gate — an alternative worth weighing: callers own a short inline elicitation step and optionally delegate to intent-lock when installed.

The misread ledger cannot compound by construction. It is runtime-written state inside the plugin tree, and marketplace installs execute from a cache copy that is replaced on update and never committed. It is forked across two repos. It holds personal data in an MIT-distributed plugin. Its only git change is 2026-07-11, although MEMORY.md logs many later runs where prior #1 fired. A rewrite should move it to a user- or project-scope path outside the plugin, with a deterministic append script (fixed grammar, verbatim Prior copied into Active priors, newest-first ordering, cap 7 with user-chosen retirement) — deterministic checks that are currently prose.

All three gate descriptions sit at 1012–1020 of 1024 chars (4, 11 and 12 chars of headroom; 1053–1082 UTF-8 bytes). Evals across the group are descriptive only (`assertions: []` in all 19 cases), decision-interview has none, no runner exists, and there are no should-trigger/should-not-trigger query sets for description optimization. Every boundary edit made so far (0.4.1, 0.4.2, 0.1.1) was therefore verified by review, not by evals.

Body sizes: intent-lock ~6.2k tokens / 245 lines (heavy rhetoric plus version-history narration), plan-critique ~2.5k tokens / 70 very long lines, decision-interview ~1.9k tokens / 87 lines, misread-capture ~1.0k tokens / 65 lines. intent-lock is the one loaded as Step 0 by five-plus other skills, so its size and its contradictions multiply across the pipeline.

inventory.group: HTML renderers / visual output plugins (clinical-infographic, concept-animation, ml-concept-lab, code-explainer, gridgeist, + learn-hub concept-animation clone)
group_level_observations: SHARED TAIL BOILERPLATE, MEASURED: the four in-house renderers (CI, CA, ML, CE) use the same section skeleton: Prime directive, Step 0 gate, Step 1-3, Step 2.5/3.5 Render & verify, Step 3/4 'Where output goes', Handoffs, Close, Failure conditions. The shared tail sections (render/verify + output + handoffs + close + failure conditions) take 67/177 body lines in CI (38%), 63/152 in CA (41%), 79/225 in ML (35%) and 56/162 in CE (35%). That is 265 lines of near-duplicate procedure in total. Exactly 28 six-word shingles appear verbatim in all four bodies, and all of them are the vault-keeper / no-filesystem / failure-condition boilerplate ('never resolve a vault path or write into vault/', 'return the HTML inline and say', 'was claimed that did not happen', '2. Surface it — show the file', 'a footer that keeps it honest', 'this skill has failed if'). Pairwise verbatim overlap is 10.0–13.0% for CI~CA and CA~ML, and 2–4% for pairs involving CE. Most duplication is paraphrased rather than verbatim, so the rule-level matrix below is the more accurate measure.

RULE RECURRENCE MATRIX (CI / CA / ML / CE / GG / learn-hub CA). (R1) Self-contained, meaning no external CSS/JS/fonts/images/CDN: stated in CI SKILL:109-110,182-183, design-system:196-204 and README:47; CA SKILL:122-123,195 and grammar:55-56; ML SKILL:176-179,275-276; CE SKILL:138-139,207, contract:123-125 and shell:110; learn-hub CA. That is 5 of 6 units, 2–4 times each. (R2) prefers-reduced-motion is mandatory in CA, ML, CE and learn-hub CA; GG mentions it; not applicable to CI. (R3) Colour never the only signal, WCAG AA, semantic headings and role=img SVG: all 5 plugins, 2–3 places each. (R4) Render headless and eyeball before hand-off: CI, CA, ML, CE and learn-hub CA. Only ML supplies a recipe, and that recipe fails as written. (R5) Fit one screen at 1366x768 with height:100dvh / 100svh: CA, ML, CE. This check is the one learn-hub proved insufficient. (R6) Honest footer: CI, CA, ML, CE. (R7) The 'illustrative — not measured data' label: CI (13 hits), CA (8). (R8) Source precedence (session, then vault-keeper query, then generate via comprehensive-review/pubmed-research-note): CI SKILL Step 0, source-contract:21-37, README:20-31 and CA SKILL:93-102. (R9) Units and qualifiers kept: CI (5 places) and CA. (R10) Intent-lock gate: CA and ML mandatory, CE conditional, CI explicitly none. (R11) Write to cwd, then surface, then file via vault-keeper as an asset, plus a 'No filesystem' paragraph: CI, CA and ML by default, CE on request only. (R12) Close with 'Two lines in chat … never restate as prose': CI, CA, ML, CE. (R13) Failure-conditions list covering self-contained, vault path, never-rendered: CI, CA, ML, CE, each 19–25 lines. (R14) Player/transport controls (Play/Pause/Restart/Prev/Next, keyboard, real buttons) plus an aria-live region: CA grammar, ML build-contract, CE contract. (R15) PNG companion deliverable: CI, CA, ML, CE.

THE LAYOUT RULE IS DUPLICATED, AND BOTH COPIES CARRY A BUG THAT WAS FIXED ONLY DOWNSTREAM. CA grammar:46 and ML build-contract:140 both prescribe `.wrap{height:100dvh}` — never min-height'. learn-hub reversed that rule on 2026-08-21: the stage collapsed on every phone for all 25 animations. The fix exists only in the learn-hub clone, and it never flowed back upstream. I ran learn-hub's own sync audit (`auditAnimationLayout` in learn-hub scripts/lib/animation-responsive.mjs) against the shipped examples. It flags `stage-can-collapse` and `children-can-shrink` on BOTH plugins/concept-animation/examples/tms-electromagnetic-induction.html AND plugins/ml-concept-lab/examples/learning-rate-and-conditioning.html. It flags nothing on the learn-hub copy of the TMS example. `auditInfographicResponsive` flags the `.mech` strip in BOTH the CI template and the CI PPGL example.

THE REAL SOURCE OF TRUTH IS EXECUTABLE CODE IN ANOTHER REPO. learn-hub ships `auditAnimationSelfContained`, `auditAnimationLayout`, `auditInfographicResponsive`, `src/lib/animation-layout.ts` (a render-time guard with floor `max(220px,min(38dvh,280px))`) and `scripts/animations/pk-plasma/verify.mjs` (whose header says 'the concept-animation skill's Step 3.5, made executable'). No plugin in this group ships a single script: none of the five has a `scripts/` directory. Every verification step is prose, and the only concrete recipe (in ML) fails as written. A rewrite should move the self-contained, layout, reduced-motion and responsive-strip checks into a shared, executable checker.

THE FILING PIPELINE IS INCOHERENT ACROSS THE TWO REPOS. CI, CA and ML file HTML into micky `vault/assets/` via vault-keeper. vault-keeper's own empty-vault skill (plugins/vault-keeper/skills/empty-vault/SKILL.md:54-56) says assets 'cannot become Learn notes. They are *removed with their topic*'. But learn-hub's ingest-infographic and ingest-animation descriptions say they fire 'when the micky-psych-tools empty-vault skill hands over an infographic/animation asset'. Meanwhile the learn-hub concept-animation clone bypasses vault-keeper entirely and writes `/vault/<topic>/<slug>.animation.md` plus the HTML, then syncs to Supabase. ML outputs actually land in learn-hub's animations table (e.g. `differentiation-three-ways.html` is cited in learn-hub vault notes as an ml-concept-lab output), yet ML's docs describe no such path.

POLICY IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS SIBLINGS. The Step 0 gate is none in CI, mandatory intent-lock in CA and ML, conditional in CE, and inlined in the learn-hub clone. Vault filing is the default in CI, CA and ML and opt-in in CE. Category is 'research' for CI, 'education' for CA, ML and CE, and 'design' for GG.

THE BOUNDARY GRAPH IS ASYMMETRIC AND TRIGGERS OVERLAP. ML's Handoffs name CA, CE, dataviz, gridgeist and firecrawl. CA names only CI and dataviz, and never mentions ML. CE never mentions ML. CA's scope includes 'algorithms, statistical ideas' and triggers on 'make an animation of X'; ML's description explicitly lists 'animate this algorithm' and 'show me how X works' as triggers, so both skills compete for algorithm animations. On clinical concepts, ML's description routes them to clinical-infographic while ML's own Handoffs and CLAUDE.md route them to concept-animation. If the micky concept-animation plugin is installed in a learn-hub session, two skills named concept-animation trigger on the same phrases ('animate this concept', '/animate') and file to different destinations.

DESCRIPTIONS ARE CROWDED AGAINST THE CAP (measured characters): CI 991, CA 1022 (1074 bytes as UTF-8), ML 997, CE 863, GG 708, learn-hub CA 1000. Four of the six are within 33 characters of the 1024 hard cap, which contradicts CLAUDE.md's 'aim well under'. Every description is third person except the learn-hub clone ('Author …', imperative). Every description puts its what-signal in the first 200 characters and has trigger phrases (Thai phrases in CI, CA, ML and CE) and a NOT-for clause.

EVALS ARE THIN. Only CI (4 cases) and CE (6 cases) have evals/evals.json, in skill-creator format. Every case has `"assertions": []` and `"files": []`, so nothing is machine-gradable and there are no fixtures. There are no should-trigger / should-not-trigger query sets. CI eval #1 depends on a vault artifact (PPGL) that no longer exists. CA, ML and GG have no evals.

DEPENDENCIES ARE NOT GUARANTEED. plugin.json has no dependency mechanism, so intent-lock, vault-keeper, comprehensive-review, pubmed-research-note and firecrawl are separate installs from the same marketplace. dataviz is not in this marketplace at all; it is an org/built-in skill. The browser tooling is assumed: Chromium exists only at /opt/pw-browsers. Playwright is installed globally only, so an ESM `import 'playwright'` from a working dir fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (measured). There is no tesseract for CI's optional OCR step.

REPO-LEVEL VALIDATION DOES NOT CATCH BROKEN LINKS. validate.py prints 'all checks passed' while CE's SKILL.md and README reference files that were never committed. It only checks name/description/version parity. It does not check intra-skill links, CHANGELOG vs version, or README file lists.

GRIDGEIST IS AN OUTLIER IN THIS GROUP. It is a vendored third-party frontend-design skill, not an HTML renderer. It has no command, README, CHANGELOG or evals. It carries an OpenAI Codex metadata file (skills/gridgeist/agents/openai.yaml) and the assets that only that file uses. CLAUDE.md's Plugins section omits it entirely, although MEMORY.md and ROUTING.md list it.

commands/refine-plugin.md (12 lines): a thin wrapper that uses $ARGUMENTS as the target. Its summary (':11-12') also leaves out the router-refresh step.

commands/route.md (25 lines): not a wrapper. It is the only implementation of routing and has no skill behind it. Its order contradicts itself: ':6 Read ROUTING.md…' comes before ':9 Before consulting the table, always run python scripts/route.py first'. It writes ROUTING.md to answer a read-only question, and it re-does the description matching that Claude Code already does natively.

defects.description: The authoring standards leave out current best practice: skill name limits (lowercase-hyphen, 64 characters max, matching the directory), the SKILL.md body-size and progressive-disclosure guidance, keeping references one level deep, allowed-tools and disable-model-invocation, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, and plugin.json `dependencies` (a field the CLI 2.1.280 validator recognizes).
defects.evidence: authoring-rules.md covers only names, versions, the catalog entry, description length and recipe, command/agent description presence, MCP url/type and folder layout (lines 6-67).

defects.description: The /route command reads ROUTING.md and then says to regenerate it first, and it writes to the repo to answer a read-only question.

strengths: A hard guard runs before any write: a kebab-case regex, a collision check against both the directory and the catalog, and 'Never overwrite' (SKILL.md:47-51).
The success claim is gated on the validator: 'Do not claim success unless it prints `all checks passed`' (SKILL.md:81-82).
It stops before commit and prints a suggested conventional commit.
Categories are discovered at runtime from marketplace.json instead of a hardcoded list (SKILL.md:38-39).
The audit has two tiers (mechanical [BLOCKER] vs [QUALITY]), each finding comes with a before/after fix, and it explicitly allows 'no findings is a valid, good result' (audit-checklist.md:71-74).
The mechanical rules have a single source, shared across both skills by a relative path, with no copy.
There is an explicit audit-only mode for targets outside this marketplace (refine SKILL.md:34-36).
The commands are thin, with correct handling of $ARGUMENTS present or absent.

units.name: vault-keeper
units.purpose: Manages the repo-root Obsidian-style vault/: files producers' outputs with frontmatter and MOC/index wiring, rebuilds indexes, and queries before saving. The empty-vault skill drains the vault into the learn-hub app through learn-hub's digest-report and deletes files only after verification.

skills.references_loaded_how: Linked five times as 'see references/vault-layout.md' / 'the single source of truth' (SKILL.md:38, :75, :84, :90, :98), with no explicit 'read X when Y' trigger. The body also restates most of the reference 'In brief' (SKILL.md:41-50), so Claude may never open it.

Format {skill_name, evals:[{id,name,prompt,expected_output,files:[],assertions:[]}]}. Every assertions array is empty and nothing runs them.

It says 'Four jobs', which is stale: plugin.json, README and the catalog say five, the fifth being the sibling skill. It does not mention filing assets or binaries (HTML infographics and animations), which many producers hand over. The first 200 characters carry the routing signal. The only 'my' words are inside quoted triggers.

units.name: firecrawl
units.purpose: Packages Firecrawl's AI-onboarding guide (install, credentials, usage paths A–F) as a skill that routes general-web data requests. Adds a marketplace contract: it is the general-web fetch engine for pubmed-research-note and comprehensive-review, Path C deliverables are gated by intent-lock, and vault saves go through vault-keeper on request.
